specCore.area: Core logic parity spec (query parsing, effort, ranking, result ids, alias resolution, gateway catalog, URL and command templating, activation, config/secrets loading and writing, signature/reload, legacy migration, restore_defaults, comment-preserving TOML editor) for the Rust rewrite of Agent Search 0.5.0. I read every file named in the task in full, plus provider.py, prompt.py, prefs.py, shortcut.py, __init__.py, docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/PROVIDERS.md for callers and contracts. I checked every non-obvious claim below by running the code under Python 3.14.8 (Unicode 16.0.0) on a scratch copy at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jem--config-Claude-scratch-workspaces-63916be0-91be-4159-8336-ddb5c5f4d763-fc68f1ac-4d0d-4c00-a3ab-97c796438bed-scratch-2026-10-18-33b1ec/c1eb6717-9f7c-4ece-a251-91a4d26833d4/scratchpad/copy, which passes all 35 tests. No project files were modified. Source paths are relative to /home/jem/Projects/git/github/oscillatingjem/gnome-llm-search-provider/src/llm_search/.

behaviors.behavior: parse(terms) walks the terms in order. The first term with len>1 that starts with '@' (while no model is set yet) sets model = term[1:].lower(). Otherwise, the first term with len>1 that starts with '!', whose term[1:].lower() is a key of EFFORT_ALIASES (while no effort is set yet), sets effort = EFFORT_ALIASES[...]. Every other term goes to words. prompt = ' '.join(words).strip(). Query is a frozen value with fields prompt, model and effort. Equality is structural.
behaviors.edge_cases:
'@' alone and '!' alone stay in the prompt. '@@x' gives model '@x'. Only the first @ token and the first valid ! token are consumed; later ones stay in the prompt ('@a @b hi' gives prompt '@b hi'; '!X !h a' gives effort max and prompt '!h a'). '!e' and '!nope' stay in the prompt; 'wow!' stays; 'bob@example.com' stays. '@x!h' gives model 'x!h'. '!XH' gives xhigh, because the match is case-insensitive. '@ÉCOLE' gives 'école'. '@İx' gives 'i̇x', 3 code points, because of the full lowercase mapping. Terms are not re-split, so a term with inner whitespace or '
' keeps it ('a
','b ' gives 'a
 b'). strip() only trims the ends, using Python whitespace. len>1 counts code points, but this is equivalent to a byte-length check for a leading ASCII '@' or '!'. Query.is_empty exists but is unused.

behaviors.behavior: Where terms come from: GNOME Shell passes them already split. The prompt box (refresh/run) splits entry text with Python str.split(). ActivateResult re-parses the terms it receives, so the prompt sent is the activation-time prompt. LaunchSearch joins the terms with ' ' and calls org.freedesktop.Application.ActivateAction('search', [<s>], {}) on the prompt-box app.
behaviors.edge_cases: str.split() with no arguments splits on every str.isspace() char. That includes \x1c-\x1f, \x85, \xa0 and  , but not ​. Verified: 'a\x1cb\x1fc\xa0d e​f\x85g' gives ['a','b','c','d','e​f','g']. Rust split_whitespace() does NOT split on \x1c-\x1f.

behaviors.behavior: EFFORTS = (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), in this order. EFFORT_ALIASES is exactly: l, lo, low → low; m, med, medium → medium; h, hi, high → high; xh, xhigh → xhigh; x, max → max.
behaviors.edge_cases: These have no alias: 'mid', 'xhi', 'mx', 'hig'. The match runs on the lowercased token.

behaviors.behavior: suggest_effort(prompt): returns 'high' if any high_effort_patterns entry matches, using re.search(p, prompt, re.IGNORECASE) evaluated in list order with short-circuit. Otherwise it counts words = len(prompt.split()) and returns 'low' if words <= low_effort_max_words, 'high' if words > 60, and 'medium' otherwise. It is called only when the query has no explicit !effort, so the patterns are not even compiled in that case.
behaviors.edge_cases: It never suggests xhigh or max. With 8 words and the default 8 → low; 9 → medium; 60 → medium; 61 → high. 'Why not' → high (pattern). If low_effort_max_words > 60, long prompts still come out low until they pass that count. An invalid pattern raises re.error at search time, but only when the patterns are evaluated.

behaviors.behavior: clamp_effort(effort, supported): returns None if effort is falsy or supported is empty. Returns effort if it is in supported. Otherwise returns min(supported, key=|EFFORTS.index(e) - EFFORTS.index(effort)|), where a name not in EFFORTS gets key 99. Ties go to the FIRST element in supported list order (Python min).
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: medium on [low,high] → low; medium on [high,low] → high; max on [low,high] → high; low on ['turbo'] → 'turbo'; xhigh on ['turbo','max'] → max. Effort names in supported are not validated; gateway variants such as 'minimal' pass through. The requested effort is always a valid EFFORTS member, so EFFORTS.index never raises.

behaviors.behavior: rank() returns [] when len(query.prompt) < config.min_chars. len counts Unicode code points, so a Rust port must use chars().count(), not len(). @ and ! tokens are already removed from the prompt.
behaviors.edge_cases: 'éé' with min_chars 3 → no rows; 'a b' → 3 chars → rows. A float min_chars (2.5) works in Python. With min_chars <= 0, an empty prompt still ranks.

behaviors.behavior: matched_tags(prompt): for each [[routing.rule]] in file order, if any pattern matches (re.search, IGNORECASE, short-circuit), then weights[tag] = weights.get(tag, 0.0) + rule.weight. The result is ordered by insertion, i.e. by the first matching rule for each tag. Several rules with the same tag add up.
behaviors.edge_cases: An integer weight 3 accumulates as 3.0. Because of the short-circuit, an invalid pattern placed after a matching one in the same rule never raises for prompts that match the earlier pattern (verified: patterns ['\\bcode\\b','('] raise only for prompts without 'code'). If patterns is a string instead of a list, Python iterates its characters, each one a regex. Example 'fast' rule '^\S+(\s+\S+){0,5}\??$': 6 words match, 7 do not.

behaviors.behavior: score(c) = c.priority + sum(w for tag, w in tags if tag in c.tags). Row.reasons = [t for t in tags (insertion order) if t in c.tags].
behaviors.edge_cases: 'in' on a list is membership. If tags were a TOML string, it becomes a SUBSTRING test (tags='coding' matches rule tag 'cod'; verified). NaN priority leaves Python's sort effectively unsorted (verified: [1, nan, 2, 0.5] stays in input order).

behaviors.behavior: Row selection: (1) If query.model is set and resolve() hits, the hit becomes row 1, built with the resolved model. (2) ranked = stable sort of the non-AUTO candidates by score, descending. Ties keep candidate-list order: gateway models in /model/info order, then apps in agents.toml order. auto = the AUTO candidates. For c in auto + ranked: break if len(rows) >= max_rows; skip c if a row with the same candidate.id already exists; otherwise append make_row(c) with model None. (3) best_app = the first APP in ranked. If it exists and no row has kind APP, rows[-1:] = [make_row(best_app)]: it replaces the last row, or appends when rows is empty.
behaviors.edge_cases: The @ row counts toward max_rows. A candidate appears only once, even with another model. With max_rows == 1, an @ hit on a gateway model or Auto is REPLACED by the best app (verified: '@coder explain this regex' with max_rows 1 → app:claude-cli). max_rows <= 0 still returns 1 row (verified for 0 and -1). The Auto row always comes right after the @ row, otherwise first. Rust: use sort_by with b.partial_cmp(a) (stable) and decide what NaN does.

behaviors.behavior: make_row(c, model=None) builds Row(candidate=c, model=model, effort=clamp_effort(query.effort or suggested, c.efforts), reasons, query_key). With no @model, app agents keep their own default model (None). The Auto candidate has no efforts, so its effort is None.
behaviors.edge_cases: The suggested effort is computed once per query and clamped per candidate. Apps without efforts get None even when the effort is explicit ('!high fix this bug').

behaviors.behavior: Row.title = candidate.name, plus ' · ' + model.capitalize() when model is set. Row.subtitle joins with ' · ' (space, U+00B7, space): f'{effort} effort' if effort, and ', '.join(reasons) if reasons. It is '' when neither is present. The provider meta description is '“' + prompt + '”' (U+201C/U+201D), plus ' · ' + subtitle when the subtitle is non-empty.
behaviors.edge_cases: Python str.capitalize titlecases the first character and LOWERCASES THE REST. Verified: 'GPT'→'Gpt', 'gpt-4o'→'Gpt-4o', 'ǆx'→'ǅx', 'ßa'→'Ssa', 'ﬁx'→'Fix', 'ŉa'→'ʼNa'. Rust std has no titlecase: char::to_uppercase('ß') = 'SS'. Example vectors: 'Claude Code (terminal) · Sonnet' / 'low effort'; 'Claude Code (terminal)' / 'max effort · coding'.

behaviors.behavior: result_id = f'{cid}|{model or ""}|{effort or ""}|{query_key}'. cid is 'app:<id>', 'model:<base>' or 'auto'. query_key = blake2s(utf8(f'{query.model or ""}\0{query.effort or ""}\0{query.prompt}'), digest_size=6).hexdigest(), giving 12 lowercase hex chars. It uses the RAW @text and the EXPLICIT effort only, not the resolved or suggested values.
behaviors.edge_cases: BLAKE2s with digest length 6 is a parameter-block setting, NOT a 32-byte digest truncated. Use blake2::Blake2s<U6> or blake2s_simd Params::hash_length(6). Vectors: Query('hello world') → 9ecaf2f6a8bf; Query('refactor this','opus','high') → edf172736af7; Query('héllo ☃') → 9a1b0be70529; parse('what should I cook tonight') → bc4896089f88; parse('@cli !x refactor the backup script') → 1f39459664cb; parse('@son write an email to bob') → 013484655309. Ids only need to be stable within one process and change with the query (GNOME caches metas by id), but matching hashes makes golden tests portable.

behaviors.behavior: parse_result_id(rid): (rid.split('|') + ['', ''])[:3] gives (cid, model or None, effort or None). The query key is ignored.
behaviors.edge_cases: 'auto' → ('auto',None,None); '' → ('',None,None); 'model:a|b|c|d|e' → ('model:a','b','c'). A '|' inside an app id, gateway base or model name silently corrupts the parse.

behaviors.behavior: resolve(name, candidates) runs in this order. (1) target = config.aliases.get(name), an exact key lookup. If target is truthy: cid, _, model = target.partition(':') (FIRST colon); return (c, model or None) for the first candidate whose id is cid, 'app:'+cid or 'model:'+cid. If none matches, fall through using the original name. (2) Exact: the first c where name is in [c.id.split(':',1)[-1], c.name.lower(), *c.aliases] → (c, None). (3) App model prefix: the first APP c with any m in c.models where m.startswith(name) → (c, the first such m in models order). (4) Prefix: the first c where any of the step-2 keys startswith(name) → (c, None). (5) None. Candidate order is gateway models (including Auto, in /model/info order) followed by apps in file order.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: '@son' → claude-cli + sonnet; '@fab' → claude-cli + fable; '@code' → alias → claude-code; '@claude-c' and '@cl' → claude-chat (first in order); '@ask' → claude-chat (name prefix); '@s' → claude-cli/sonnet, because step 3 runs before step 4; '@b' → model:big. Alias 'y'='claude-cli:opus' → claude-cli/opus. 'z'='auto' → Auto. 'w'='big:foo' → model:big with model 'foo' (title 'Big · Foo'; the URL ignores it). 'x'='app:claude-cli' → cid 'app' → no match (bug). Alias targets pointing at hidden apps fall through. [aliases] KEYS are never prefix-matched. App ids, gateway bases and app models are compared case-sensitively against the lowercased name. App candidates have no aliases; only gateway models carry model_info.aliases (lowercased).

behaviors.behavior: app_candidates(config): for each a in config.apps in file order, when a.enabled is truthy AND every entry in a.requires resolves via which(), build Candidate(id='app:'+a.id, kind='app', name, tags, efforts, models, icon, priority). The candidate has no aliases.
behaviors.edge_cases: Empty requires means available. Python truthiness: enabled=0 or '' hides the row; enabled='false' (a string) SHOWS it. Lists are shared by reference with App.

behaviors.behavior: models_from_info(data, auto_model): for each entry, name = entry.get('model_name','') and info = entry.get('model_info') or {}. If name == auto_model: by_base[name] = Candidate(id='auto', kind='auto', name=info.get('display_name','Auto'), tags=info.get('tags',[]), icon='emblem-system-symbolic'), then continue. Otherwise base = info.get('base') or name. The FIRST entry for a base creates Candidate(id='model:'+base, kind='model', name=info.get('display_name', base), tags=info.get('tags',[]), aliases=[a.lower() for a in info.get('aliases',[])], icon=info.get('icon','user-available-symbolic'), priority=info.get('priority',0.0)). Every entry for the base, the first included, appends info['effort'] to efforts if it is truthy and not already present. Output order is dict insertion order of first appearance; an overwrite keeps the original position.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: a later entry with base == auto_model adds its effort to the Auto candidate. A missing model_name gives id 'model:'. display_name: null gives name None, because the .get default applies only to MISSING keys. tags: null makes the later 'in' raise TypeError. Unknown effort strings ('minimal') are kept. Integer priority stays an integer. The first entry decides display_name, tags, aliases, icon and priority; later entries only add efforts.

behaviors.behavior: Gateway.models(): returns [] if litellm_url is empty. It returns the cached list when now - fetched < 60 s or now - failed < 30 s (time.monotonic, both initialized to 0.0). Otherwise it sends GET litellm_url + '/model/info' with timeout 0.5 s, adding 'Authorization: Bearer <secrets[key_env]>' only when that secret is non-empty. It parses the body with json.load, takes .get('data', []) and calls models_from_info. On success it sets fetched=now. On OSError or ValueError it sets models=[] and failed=now. candidates() = gateway.models() + app_candidates(config). Each config reload creates a new Gateway, which resets the cache. The key is read only from secrets.env, never from the process environment.
behaviors.edge_cases: In the first 60 s after boot, no fetch happens, because monotonic minus 0.0 is under 60. Use Option<Instant> in Rust. Caught: URLError, HTTPError, timeout, connection reset, JSONDecodeError, unknown url type. NOT caught: a non-dict JSON body (AttributeError), non-dict entries, http.client.IncompleteRead. Those propagate and fail the search. The timeout applies per socket operation, so DNS is not bounded. The call blocks the D-Bus handler and the prompt box's GTK main thread. A '#fragment' in url swallows '/model/info'.
behaviors.covered_by_test: none (models_from_info is tested; the HTTP path and caching are not)

behaviors.behavior: fill(template, **values): (1) Run template.format(**{k: quote(v or '', safe='')}). Everything except A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . - ~ is percent-encoded as UTF-8 with uppercase hex, and space becomes %20. (2) parts = urlsplit(url). If parts.query is empty, return url unchanged. (3) Take the pairs from parse_qsl(query, keep_blank_values=True), drop every pair whose DECODED value is empty, rebuild the query with urlencode(pairs, quote_via=quote) (safe='' for both keys and values), and return urlunsplit.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified vectors: 'claude://claude.ai/new?q={prompt}' + 'hello & goodbye?' → 'claude://claude.ai/new?q=hello%20%26%20goodbye%3F'. 'x://new?model={model}' with no model → 'x://new' (the '?' is dropped). '?q={prompt}&flag&x=' → '?q=p' (key-only params dropped). Literal template parts get re-normalized: '+' → %20, '/' → %2F (doc example folder=/home/you/... → folder=%2Fhome%2Fyou%2FProjects%2Fmy-app), '%FF' → %EF%BF%BD, '%zz' → %25zz, ';' and '=' in values → %3B/%3D, a literal space → %20, '&&' collapsed. An empty fragment '#' is dropped; '#frag' is kept. When a query exists, the scheme is lowercased ('Claude://Host/Path?q=' → 'claude://Host/Path?q='); a URL with no query keeps its case. 'x://?q=' → 'x:?q=' because the empty netloc drops '//'. 'http:/path?q=' → 'http:///path?q='. Leading whitespace is stripped; trailing whitespace is kept and encoded. Duplicate keys and their order are kept. str.format semantics leak: '{{x}}' → '{x}' (then %7B/%7D in the query); '{prompt:.2}' truncates; '{prompt!r}' adds quotes; '{prompt.upper}' leaks a method repr; '{0}' → IndexError; an unknown name → KeyError; a lone '{' → ValueError. All of these surface at activation.

behaviors.behavior: url_for(config, cid, model, effort, prompt): kind, _, name = cid.partition(':'). APP: app = the first config.apps entry with id == name (ignores enabled and requires); returns fill(app.url, prompt=, model=, effort=) if app.url, else None. Otherwise, returns None if chat_url is empty. AUTO: fill(chat_url, model=auto_model, prompt=), with NO effort key. MODEL: fill(chat_url, model=gateway_model_id(name, effort), prompt=), where gateway_model_id = f'{base}@{effort}' if effort else base. Any other kind → None.
behaviors.edge_cases: '{effort}' in chat_url raises KeyError for both Auto and model rows. A model chosen through an alias on a gateway row is ignored. With model:big + effort high + chat_url 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/?models={model}&q={prompt}' the result is '...?models=big%40high&q=hi'. Auto gives models=smart-router. A base containing ':' survives, because partition splits at the first colon.

behaviors.behavior: fill_command(template, prompt, model, effort): PLACEHOLDER = r'\{(\w+)\}' (Unicode \w). Each top-level item is a group: a list item as-is, anything else wrapped as [item]. Each part is str(part). render(part) returns None if ANY placeholder name found in it maps to a missing or empty value; otherwise it replaces each {name} with the value verbatim in one pass, so values are never re-scanned. A group goes into argv only if every part rendered. Items without placeholders are always kept.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: an unknown name such as {foo} is always dropped. '{{prompt}}' → '{P}' (no brace escaping). 'x{prompt}y{model}' → 'xPyM'. '' is kept as an empty argument. Non-string parts: 5→'5', True→'True', 1.5→'1.5', and a nested list deeper than one level becomes its Python repr "['c']". A prompt containing '{model}' or shell metacharacters is passed through as one argument. ['{prompt}'] with an empty prompt → [].

behaviors.behavior: command_for(app, model, effort, prompt): argv = fill_command(...). resolved = {p: which(p) for p in app.requires}. EVERY argv element exactly equal to a requires entry is replaced by its resolved path, when one was found. cwd = str(Path(app.cwd).expanduser()). Returns (argv, cwd).
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: prompt 'claude' becomes '/usr/bin/claude' (bug), and so does a model equal to 'ptyxis'. cwd '' → '.' (the process cwd); '~/Projects/' → '/home/u/Projects'; 'a//b/./c' → 'a/b/c'; '~nosuchuser' → RuntimeError. A path containing '/' in requires is checked directly.

behaviors.behavior: which(program) = shutil.which(program, path=os.pathsep.join([$PATH or '', expanduser('~/.local/bin'), expanduser('~/bin')])). A name containing '/' is checked as given. Otherwise each directory is tried in order, with duplicates skipped. A hit must exist, be X_OK and not be a directory. The joined path is returned without canonicalization.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: with PATH unset, the leading empty entry resolves the name relative to the process cwd ('fakeprog' found). which('./fakeprog') → './fakeprog'. A directory name → None. expanduser uses $HOME, then falls back to pwd. Tests monkeypatch launch.which so every name is found at '/usr/bin/<name>' except names starting with 'missing-'. A Rust port needs the same injection seam.

behaviors.behavior: activate(config, result_id, prompt): parse the id. app = the first config.apps entry with 'app:'+id == cid (no enabled check). If app.copy_prompt, copy the prompt to the clipboard FIRST. If app.command is non-empty: build (argv, cwd), log 'running %s in %s' % (argv[0], cwd), run_command, return; the url is ignored. Otherwise url = url_for(...). If it is truthy, log 'opening ' + url.split('?')[0] and call Gio.AppInfo.launch_default_for_uri(url, None). Otherwise do nothing. The logger is named 'llm-search'.
behaviors.edge_cases: An empty argv after filling raises IndexError at the log line. A missing cwd raises FileNotFoundError from Popen. copy_prompt with neither command nor url only copies. Gateway and Auto rows never copy.

behaviors.behavior: run_command: subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=cwd, start_new_session=True (setsid), stdin, stdout and stderr = /dev/null, close_fds=True). The environment is inherited. EXTRA_PATH is NOT added to the child's PATH; only argv items that match requires are absolutized. The process is never waited on.
behaviors.edge_cases: Python reaps finished children on the next Popen. A Rust port in the resident prompt box must reap them (a waiter thread or SIGCHLD) or double-fork to avoid zombies. Use CommandExt::process_group(0) or setsid in pre_exec.

behaviors.behavior: copy_to_clipboard(text): if shutil.which('wl-copy') finds it on the default PATH, run ['wl-copy','--',text] and wait for it. Otherwise, if xclip is found, run ['xclip','-selection','clipboard'] with the UTF-8 text on stdin. check=False. If neither exists, nothing happens.
behaviors.edge_cases: EXTRA_PATH is not used here. Exit status is ignored.

behaviors.behavior: home() = Path($LLM_SEARCH_HOME) if the variable is non-empty, else Path.home()/'.llm-search'. config_dir() = home/'config'. state_dir() = home/'state'.
behaviors.edge_cases: The value is used verbatim, with NO '~' expansion ('~/rel' gives the literal relative path '~/rel/config'); relative paths are relative to the cwd. An empty variable means the default. state_dir is unused in Python. The D-Bus .service files pass LLM_SEARCH_HOME=@HOME@.

behaviors.behavior: load(directory=None): dir = directory or config_dir(). Runs migrate_legacy_settings(dir), then reads agents.toml with tomllib; a missing file gives {}. Builds Config with: min_chars = search.min_chars (default 3); max_rows = search.max_rows (5); apps = [App(**t) for t in data['app']]; aliases = {k.lower(): v}; rules = [Rule(**r) for r in routing.rule]; high_effort_patterns = routing.high_effort_patterns ([]); low_effort_max_words = routing.low_effort_max_words (8); litellm_url = gateway.url ('').rstrip('/'); litellm_key_env = gateway.key_env ('LITELLM_MASTER_KEY'); chat_url = gateway.chat_url (''); auto_model = gateway.auto_model ('smart-router'); prompt_idle_minutes = prompt.idle_minutes (30.0); secrets = read_env_file(dir/'secrets.env'); directory = dir. App defaults: url '', command [], cwd '~', requires [], description '', icon 'system-search-symbolic', tags/models/efforts [], priority 0.0, copy_prompt False, enabled True. Rule default: weight 1.0.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: an unknown key in [[app]] or [[routing.rule]], or a missing id, name, tag or patterns, raises TypeError, and the whole load fails. Unknown top-level tables and keys are ignored. Types are not checked: min_chars=2.5 works; an integer priority or weight is fine; strings fail later, at rank time. Alias key collisions after lowercasing: the last one wins ({Foo, foo} → foo's value). Alias values are not lowercased. 'http://h:1///' → 'http://h:1'. Errors that propagate: TOMLDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, PermissionError, and anything from the legacy migration. App.description is loaded but unused. A Rust port deserializing with serde must accept integer-or-float for priority, weight and idle_minutes, and decide whether to keep accepting floats for min_chars and max_rows.

behaviors.behavior: read_env_file(path): read_text, returning {} on OSError. For each line from str.splitlines(): strip it; skip it if empty, if it starts with '#', or if it has no '='. Split at the first '=': key = left.strip(), value = right.strip().strip("'\""). A later duplicate overrides an earlier one.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: A = 'quoted' → quoted. C='"mixed"' → mixed: every leading and trailing quote character is stripped independently, unpaired too. D=a=b → 'a=b'. 'E=v # not comment' keeps the comment text. '  F  =  spaced  ' → F=spaced. '=novalue' gives the empty key ''. 'export H=1' gives key 'export H'. 'I=' → ''. 'K=""' → ''. splitlines also splits on \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85,  ,   and \r (verified 'A=1\x0bB=2 C=3'). Invalid UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is NOT caught, so config load fails. The encoding is the locale encoding.

behaviors.behavior: set_secret(key, value, directory): lines = read_text().splitlines() ([] if the file is missing). Keep every line whose ln.strip().partition('=')[0].strip() != key. If value is non-empty, append f'{key}={value}' at the END. Write '\n'.join(kept) + '\n' through os.open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o600), then os.chmod(path, 0o600).
behaviors.edge_cases:
Verified: 'A=1
K=old
B=2
  K = dup
K
# K=commented
export K=x
' with K=new gives 'A=1
B=2
# K=commented
export K=x
K=new
'. Every K line is removed (including a bare 'K' and an indented ' K = dup'); commented lines and 'export K' are kept; CRLF becomes LF; the key moves to the end. Removing a key from a missing file creates a file containing just '
'. The value is written raw: no quoting, and newlines are not rejected. Not atomic: a truncate followed by a write. An existing 0644 file holds the new secret at 0644 until the chmod. The directory must exist.

behaviors.behavior: signature(directory) = a tuple, for agents.toml and then secrets.env, of (st_mtime_ns, st_size), or None when the file is missing (FileNotFoundError only). stat follows symlinks. Reload triggers: the provider compares the signature on EVERY search and, if it changed, runs load() and creates a new Gateway. The prompt box compares it in open(). The settings window watches agents.toml with Gio monitor_file(WATCH_MOVES), debounces by 300 ms, compares signature(self.directory) with app.signature, and on a difference reloads, rebuilds its pages and shows the toast 'Updated from agents.toml'. Its own saves call app.reload(), which records the new signature, so they never trigger the refresh.
behaviors.edge_cases: A missing directory gives (None, None). If load() raises during a reload, the signature is not updated, so the next search retries; meanwhile the search returns a D-Bus error. Two same-size edits within one timestamp tick go unnoticed. PermissionError on stat propagates. settings.toml is not part of the signature (docs say 'three files').

behaviors.behavior: update(edits, directory): path = dir/'agents.toml'; text = read_text() ('' if missing); new = toml_edit.apply(text, edits). If new == text, return without writing. Otherwise write dir/'.agents.toml.tmp'; if agents.toml exists, chmod the temp file to its mode & 0o777; then tmp.replace(path), an atomic rename.
behaviors.edge_cases:
Verified: mode 0640 is kept. A missing file is created at the umask mode (0644) with the content '
[search]  # added by the settings window
min_chars = 4
'. A symlinked agents.toml is REPLACED by a regular file, and the link target is left unchanged (verified). No fsync. The temp file name is fixed, so concurrent writers race. An [[app]] edit against a missing file raises EditError. Raises EditError (a ValueError subclass) or OSError, and on failure the file is untouched.

behaviors.behavior: migrate_legacy_settings(dir): data = _read_toml(dir/'settings.toml') ({} if missing), then return if the file doesn't exist. Edits are, in order: for table in (search, prompt, routing, gateway), each (table, key, None, value) in that table's key order; then, for each app_id in data['app'] (the 0.4.0 shape [app."<id>"]), each ("app", key, app_id, value) whose key is enabled, priority or cwd. update(edits, dir). On EditError or OSError, return and leave the legacy file in place. Otherwise rename it to settings.toml.migrated. Runs at the start of EVERY load().
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: an invalid settings.toml raises TOMLDecodeError out of load(), so the whole config fails, every time. Array values such as routing.high_effort_patterns, or an unknown app id, make the migration abort silently; the file stays, and it is retried and fails again on every load. Legacy app keys other than the three are dropped silently. An empty settings.toml still runs apply([]), which validates agents.toml, and then it is renamed. Missing [gateway] keys are appended in REVERSE order (chat_url above url). A gateway url keeps its trailing '/' in the file (load strips it). An existing settings.toml.migrated is overwritten.

behaviors.behavior: restore_defaults(dir) = update([('search','min_chars',None,3), ('search','max_rows',None,5), ('prompt','idle_minutes',None,30.0), ('routing','low_effort_max_words',None,8)], dir). The values come from the Config() field defaults through the GENERAL map. Agents, aliases, rules, the gateway and the shortcut are untouched.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: on the pristine example, the only diff is '- idle_minutes = 30' / '+ idle_minutes = 30.0', because the factory value is the float 30.0, formatted with repr. A second restore is a no-op. The settings window's spin row writes idle_minutes as an int, so these alternate. The settings window then closes and reopens with the toast 'Defaults restored'.

behaviors.behavior: format_value(v): bool → 'true'/'false', checked BEFORE int. int or float → repr(v). str → json.dumps(v) with ensure_ascii=True. Anything else → EditError(f"can't write {type(v).__name__} values").
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified repr: 30.0→'30.0', 2.5→'2.5', 0.1→'0.1', 1e16→'1e+16', 1e15→'1000000000000000.0', 1e-5→'1e-05', 0.0001→'0.0001', -0.0→'-0.0', inf→'inf', nan→'nan' (the readback then fails because nan != nan), 0.30000000000000004 kept; 2**70 → full digits. json.dumps: 'é'→"é"; '😀'→"😀", which TOML rejects ('Escaped character is not a Unicode scalar value'), so EditError; control chars → \u0001; DEL → \u007f; '/' is not escaped; \n \t \" \\ use short forms. None → "can't write NoneType values"; list → "can't write list values".

behaviors.behavior: Header detection: HEADER = r'^\s*(\[\[?)\s*([A-Za-z0-9_.\"\' -]+?)\s*(\]\]?)\s*(#.*)?$' is matched against each line. A line is a header only if (group1 == '[[') == (group3 == ']]'). The name is group(2).strip(), compared LITERALLY, quotes and inner spaces included. _headers() returns (index, name, is_array) for every line, with no awareness of multi-line strings or arrays.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: '  [ search ]   # hi' is the header 'search'. '[[app]' and '[app]]' are rejected. '["search"]' has the name '"search"', which is not 'search', so a new [search] gets appended and the edit fails as a duplicate table. '[a . b]' has the name 'a . b'. A multi-line array line consisting of exactly '  ["--v"]' is detected as a header named '"--v"' (verified), and so is '[search]' inside a """ string. That truncates spans and causes spurious EditErrors; it is safe only because of the readback check (T-09).

behaviors.behavior: _span(lines, start) is the index of the next header line after start, of ANY name or kind, or len(lines). Key search and insertion happen only inside [header+1, span).
behaviors.edge_cases: A sub-table header such as [app.env] ends an [[app]] span.

behaviors.behavior: _key_line(key) = r'^(\s*)' + re.escape(key) + r'(\s*=\s*)(.*)$'. It matches only a BARE key at the start of a line (indentation allowed); group 2 is the exact separator, kept as-is.
behaviors.edge_cases: These do not match: quoted keys ('"min_chars" = 3', which then fails as 'Cannot overwrite a value'), dotted keys ('search.min_chars = 3', which fails as 'Cannot declare (search) twice') and commented lines ('# min_chars = 3', so the key counts as missing). 'id' does not match 'idle_minutes'. 'min_chars=3' matches with the separator '='.

behaviors.behavior: _split_value(rest): the cut points are the index of every '#' in rest, in order, plus len(rest). For each cut, candidate = rest[:cut].rstrip(). The FIRST non-empty candidate that parses as a complete TOML value (tomllib.loads('x = ' + candidate) succeeds) returns (candidate, rest[len(candidate):]); the remainder keeps its whitespace and comment exactly. If none parses, return None: the value continues on following lines.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: '"a#b"  # c # d' → value '"a#b"' and suffix '  # c # d'. '3   ' → suffix '   '. '[1, 2]  # arr' is complete and gets replaced by a scalar. '{a = 1}' is complete and gets replaced. '[1,' → None → EditError(f'{key} is a multi-line value; edit it in the file'). rstrip uses Python whitespace; TOML whitespace is space and tab only. Completeness depends on tomllib (TOML 1.0) accepting the value; the Rust TOML parser decides this in a port.

behaviors.behavior: _set_in_span: replaces the FIRST line in the span that matches the key with indent + key + original separator + format_value(v) + original suffix. If the key is not in the span, it inserts the unindented line f'{key} = {format_value(v)}' at index (insert_after if given, else header) + 1, i.e. directly below the header, or directly below the id line for [[app]] items.
behaviors.edge_cases:
Verified: 'priority = 1.0        # the default choice...' → 'priority = 2.0        # the default choice...', with alignment kept. '  min_chars=3#c' → '  min_chars=4#c'. A missing key goes ABOVE the table's existing blank lines, comments and keys: '[search]
min_chars = 4

# comment
max_rows = 5'. The toml_edit crate appends new keys at the END of the table by default, so the position differs unless handled explicitly.

behaviors.behavior: set_table_value(text, table, key, v): lines = text.splitlines(). On the first non-array header whose name == table, run _set_in_span. If there is none, append ['', f'[{table}]  # added by the settings window', f'{key} = {fv}']. Return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'.
behaviors.edge_cases:
Verified: two edits to a missing table in one call → '[gateway]  # added by the settings window
chat_url = "b"
url = "a"': the later edit goes ABOVE the earlier one. The table name is inserted raw, without quoting. Editing table 'app' when only [[app]] exists appends [app], which fails as 'Cannot declare (app) twice'. An empty file becomes '
[search]  # added by the settings window
min_chars = 5
'. A commented-out '# [gateway]' block is ignored, and a new table is appended at the end of the file.

behaviors.behavior: set_array_item_value(text, array, item_id, key, v): for each array header (is_array) whose name == array, scan its span for lines matching _key_line('id') whose _split_value value parses (tomllib 'x = <value>')['x'] to a value == item_id, then run _set_in_span with insert_after set to that id line. If no entry matches, raise EditError(f'no [[{array}]] with id {item_id!r}').
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: the id does not need to be the first key. A missing key is inserted right after the id line ('id = "a"  # the id\nenabled = false\ncwd = "~/x"'), and for an id on the first line it lands above name. The message uses Python repr: "no [[app]] with id 'zz'". An integer id 1 does not equal '1'. If ids are duplicated, the first block wins. Only 'app' is used today; [[routing.rule]] has no id, so rules can't be edited.

behaviors.behavior: apply(text, edits): applies each edit in order, as (table, key, None, v) for a [table] or (table, key, id, v) for an [[table]] item. Then it parses the WHOLE result with tomllib; on failure it raises EditError('the edit would break the file: <tomllib message>'). Then, for each edit, it reads the value back: data.get(table,{}).get(key), or the key of the first item in data[table] whose id == item_id. If got != v (Python ==), it raises EditError(f'{table}.{key} reads back as {got!r}, not {v!r}'). It returns the new text and never writes.
behaviors.edge_cases: An already invalid file fails ANY edit, including apply([]). Two edits to the same key fail ('reads back as 5, not 4'). Python == lets True==1==1.0, so the check is type-lenient: writing True into min_chars passes, and 1.0 replaces an int. A dotted table name 'a.b' always fails the readback. The tomllib error text appears in toasts. The verification also catches the fake-header and duplicate-insert cases.

behaviors.behavior: Line normalization on every apply: the text is split with str.splitlines() and joined with '\n', and a single trailing '\n' is added. Every edit therefore converts CRLF and lone CR to LF and adds a missing final newline. Trailing blank lines survive.
behaviors.edge_cases: Verified: a literal   or \x85 inside a TOML string splits that line, so ANY edit to such a file fails with EditError ('Illegal character'). A CRLF file is rewritten as LF even when the value is unchanged, because new != text.

behaviors.behavior: Keys the current settings window writes, with types: [search] min_chars and max_rows (int, spin ranges 1-20 and 1-10); [prompt] idle_minutes (int, 0-480 step 5); [routing] low_effort_max_words (int, 0-50); [gateway] url, chat_url and auto_model (stripped str; an empty url disables the gateway); [[app]] enabled (bool), priority (float, -10..10 step 0.5, 1 digit) and cwd (stripped str; '' is saved as '~'; the folder picker replaces a home prefix with '~'). secrets.env[key_env] gets the stripped value; empty removes it. Error toasts read "Couldn't save: <msg>". Idle timer: minutes <= 0 quits at once; otherwise timeout_add_seconds(int(minutes*60)).
behaviors.edge_cases: The folder picker's home-prefix test is a plain startswith, so '/home/jem2/x' becomes '~2/x'. The gateway Test button fetches synchronously on the GTK thread. A spin row clamps out-of-range file values only for display.

external_contracts: D-Bus search provider: bus name io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider, object path /io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch/SearchProvider, interface org.gnome.Shell.SearchProvider2. Methods: GetInitialResultSet(as terms)->as; GetSubsearchResultSet(as previous, as terms)->as (previous is ignored and a full search runs); GetResultMetas(as ids)->aa{sv} with keys id, name, description and gicon (a string from Gio.ThemedIcon.new(icon).to_string()), where ids not in the last search are skipped; ActivateResult(s id, as terms, u timestamp); LaunchSearch(as terms, u timestamp). Errors: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed (str(exception)) and org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownMethod. The service is a G_APPLICATION_IS_SERVICE with a 60000 ms inactivity timeout.

Search provider .ini: DesktopId=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.desktop, BusName as above, ObjectPath as above, Version=2. GNOME reads it only from system data dirs, so the installer adds ~/.llm-search/state/xdg through ~/.config/environment.d/60-llm-search.conf.

Prompt box: application id io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch at object path /io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch (DBusActivatable). Actions: 'search' (s) and 'preferences'. It is started with --gapplication-service. The provider calls org.freedesktop.Application.ActivateAction('search', [<s joined terms>], {}).
D-Bus .service Exec lines set the env vars LLM_SEARCH_HOME=@HOME@ and PYTHONPATH. The Rust Exec must keep passing LLM_SEARCH_HOME.
Result id format: '<cid>|<model>|<effort>|<12-hex blake2s-48 query key>', where cid is 'app:<id>', 'model:<base>' or 'auto'.
Row title 'Name · Model' (U+00B7) and subtitle '<effort> effort · tag, tag'. Meta description '“<prompt>” · <subtitle>'.
Env var LLM_SEARCH_HOME: an empty value means the default $HOME/.llm-search; no ~ expansion. HOME and PATH are also read.

Files: $LLM_SEARCH_HOME/config/agents.toml; config/secrets.env (forced to mode 0600); config/settings.toml (legacy 0.4.0), renamed to settings.toml.migrated; config/.agents.toml.tmp (the temp file for atomic writes); $LLM_SEARCH_HOME/state/ (install, xdg).

agents.toml schema: [search] min_chars=3, max_rows=5; [prompt] idle_minutes=30; [[app]] id*, name*, url, command (argv list with nested optional groups), cwd='~', requires, description, icon='system-search-symbolic', tags, models, efforts, priority=0.0, copy_prompt=false, enabled=true; [aliases] name = 'app-id' | 'app-id:model' | 'gateway-model'; [gateway] url, key_env='LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', chat_url, auto_model='smart-router'; [routing] low_effort_max_words=8, high_effort_patterns=[]; [[routing.rule]] tag*, patterns*, weight=1.0. Unknown keys in [[app]] or [[routing.rule]] currently fail the load.
Placeholders {prompt}, {model} and {effort}: url templates are percent-encoded; command templates are inserted raw. chat_url receives only {model} and {prompt}.
Search syntax: @name, and !level with low/medium/high/xhigh/max and the short forms l lo m med h hi xh x.
Per-user binary search dirs EXTRA_PATH: ~/.local/bin and ~/bin, appended after $PATH.

Gateway HTTP: GET <url>/model/info with 'Authorization: Bearer <secrets.env[key_env]>'. Response {'data':[{'model_name', 'model_info':{display_name, tags, aliases, base, effort, icon, priority}}]}. The chat model id for variants is '<base>@<effort>', which the LiteLLM model_name must follow.
Icons: apps default to 'system-search-symbolic', gateway models to 'user-available-symbolic', Auto is 'emblem-system-symbolic'.
Clipboard tools: 'wl-copy -- <text>', or 'xclip -selection clipboard' with stdin.
Comment marker on tables the editor appends: '[<table>]  # added by the settings window'.

Keyboard shortcut: GNOME custom keybinding at /org/gnome/settings-daemon/plugins/media-keys/custom-keybindings/llm-search/ (schema org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys.custom-keybinding). Keys: name 'Agent Search', command '<home>/.local/bin/llm-search prompt', binding. The path is listed in org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys custom-keybindings.
Log lines (logger 'llm-search', format '%(name)s: %(message)s'): 'running <argv0> in <cwd>' and 'opening <url before ?>'.
CLI bin/llm-search query calls GetInitialResultSet via gdbus. 'llm-search test' runs the Python unittest suite, so it will need a Rust equivalent (cargo test) or a wrapper.
python_specific_semantics: User routing patterns (high_effort_patterns, [[routing.rule]].patterns) run through Python re.search(p, prompt, re.IGNORECASE) on str: an unanchored search, compiled lazily at search time and cached by the re module. Neither the Rust regex crate nor fancy-regex reproduces this exactly. fancy-regex adds lookaround, backrefs, atomic groups and possessive quantifiers, but delegates to regex for \w, \b and \s, so the Unicode differences below remain. Recommendation: compile every pattern at load time with '(?i)' prepended, report errors with the rule index, and keep a corpus test of the shipped patterns.

Python \w = str.isalnum() or '_'; Rust \w = Alphabetic + Mark + Nd + Pc + Join_Control. Verified in Python: combining U+0301 is NOT \w; '²', '½' and 'Ⅻ' ARE \w; '‿' (U+203F) and ZWJ are NOT. Consequences for \b: Python matches '\bcafe\b' in 'café' (Rust does not, because the mark is \w there), and Python does NOT match '\bgit\b' in 'git²' (Rust does).
Python \s includes \x1c-\x1f and \x85/\xa0, but not ​ or ᠎; Rust \s (White_Space) lacks \x1c-\x1f. \d is Unicode Nd in both.

Python IGNORECASE: 'İ' and 'i' match each other in both directions, 'k' matches 'K' (U+212A), 's' matches 'ſ', 'σ' matches 'ς', 'ß' matches 'ẞ', 'ss' does not match 'ß'. Rust (?i) uses simple case folding, under which U+0130 likely does NOT match 'i'. Verify in Rust.

Python '$' (without MULTILINE) also matches before a final '\n' ('x$' matches 'x\n'); Rust '$' matches only at the end. Python \Z means end of string; Rust has no \Z (it is a syntax error) and uses \z. Python 3.14 also accepts \z.

Syntax Python accepts but Rust regex rejects: lookbehind and lookahead ((?<=, (?=, (?!, (?<!), backrefs (\1, (?P=n)), possessive quantifiers (a++), atomic groups ((?>...)), conditionals, \N{NAME}, octal \0 escapes, a literal 'a{3', a bare '{'. Behaves differently: '[[:alpha:]]' is a nested-set literal in Python (it matches '[', ':', 'a'... followed by ']'), but a POSIX class in Rust. Rust accepts but Python rejects: \p{L}, (?<name>...), and global flags in mid-pattern ('a(?i)b' is an error in Python 3.11+). Python accepts 'a{,3}' as {0,3}; check Rust.

The pattern-evaluation order is observable: any() short-circuits, and high_effort_patterns run only when no !effort is given. So invalid patterns fail only for some prompts today. A failure raises out of rank(): the provider returns a D-Bus error and the prompt box shows no rows.

str.split() (no args), str.strip() and str.rstrip() use str.isspace() (it includes \x1c-\x1f). str.splitlines() also breaks on \v, \f, \x1c-\x1e, \x85,  ,   and a lone \r. Rust lines() breaks only on \n and \r\n.

len() counts code points (min_chars). str.lower() uses the full Unicode lowercase mapping, including final sigma ('İ' → 'i̇'). str.capitalize() titlecases the first char and lowercases the rest ('GPT'→'Gpt', 'ǆ'→'ǅ', 'ß'→'Ss'); Rust std has no titlecase.
str.startswith, the 'in' operator (substring when the operand is a str), str.partition (first separator only) and str.split('|') (all separators).
hashlib.blake2s(digest_size=6): the digest length lives in the parameter block, so this is not a truncated BLAKE2s-256.

json.dumps(str) with ensure_ascii=True: non-ASCII → \uXXXX, astral chars → surrogate-pair escapes (invalid in TOML, so EditError), control chars → \u00XX with short forms for \b \f \n \r \t, DEL → \u007f, '/' unescaped. serde_json writes raw UTF-8 instead, and toml_edit picks literal or basic quoting automatically. Either gives a byte-level difference.

repr(float) is the shortest round-trip form and switches to exponent notation at >= 1e16 or < 1e-4, with a 2-digit signed exponent ('1e+16', '1e-05', '-0.0', 'inf', 'nan'). Rust {} prints '30' for 30.0 and never uses an exponent; Rust {:?} prints '30.0', '1e16' and 'NaN', and 'NaN' is invalid TOML. restore_defaults depends on '30.0'. repr(int) has arbitrary precision. bool is checked before int because bool is a subclass of int.
Python == in the readback check: 1 == 1.0 == True, nan != nan.

tomllib implements TOML 1.0, accepts arbitrary-size ints, and produces its own error messages (shown in toasts). It decides _is_complete for values, so a Rust TOML parser that accepts TOML 1.1 (newlines in inline tables, \e, \xHH) changes which values count as single-line.

str.format mini-language in url and chat_url templates: '{{'/'}}' escapes, format specs ('{prompt:.2}'), conversions ('!r'), attribute access, and positional '{0}' raising IndexError, an unknown name raising KeyError, a lone '{' raising ValueError.

urllib.parse: quote(v, safe='') keeps only ALPHA, DIGIT and '_.-~', using UTF-8 and uppercase hex. urlsplit lowercases the scheme, lstrips C0 control and space chars, and deletes \t\r\n. parse_qsl splits on '&' only, turns '+' into a space, percent-decodes with errors='replace' and skips empty pairs. urlencode(quote_via=quote) uses safe='', so '/' becomes %2F. urlunsplit drops an empty query or fragment, drops '//' for an empty netloc on non-netloc schemes ('x://?q=' → 'x:?q='), and adds '//' for uses_netloc schemes ('http:/p' → 'http:///p'). The Rust url crate (WHATWG) differs in all of these, so implement the pipeline by hand.

shutil.which: an empty PATH entry means the cwd, a name containing '/' is checked directly, the hit must pass X_OK and not be a directory, duplicates are skipped, and the joined path is returned. os.path.expanduser uses $HOME first, then pwd. Path('').expanduser() is '.', and Path normalization removes trailing '/' and '.' components. '~user' is expanded; an unknown home raises RuntimeError.
Python sorted(key, reverse=True) is stable: equal keys keep their input order. NaN keys break the ordering silently. min() returns the first minimum (the clamp_effort tie-break).

dict insertion order is part of the output: matched_tags gives the order of reasons; models_from_info keeps a key's first position when it is overwritten; a lowercase alias collision means the last one wins.

dataclass App(**table) and Rule(**table) reject unknown and missing keys (TypeError) but never check types. Python truthiness: enabled = 0 or '' is false, while 'false' as a string is true. str(part) for non-string command items gives 'True', '1.5' and "['c']".
time.monotonic() starts the cache timestamps at 0.0, so nothing is fetched in the first 60 s after boot.
Path.read_text, write_text and os.fdopen use the locale encoding (UTF-8 on Fedora; Rust is always UTF-8). os.open's mode is subject to the umask. os.replace swaps a symlink for a regular file.
subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True, close_fds=True, DEVNULL) and implicit zombie reaping on later Popen calls. urllib's timeout applies per socket operation. json.load auto-detects UTF-8/16/32.

Exceptions caught in the gateway are OSError and ValueError, including URLError, HTTPError, socket timeout, JSONDecodeError and 'unknown url type' ValueError. AttributeError and http.client.HTTPException subclasses such as IncompleteRead escape.
bugs_or_gaps_found: Ranker: with max_rows == 1, an explicit @gateway-model or @auto row is replaced by the best app agent (verified: '@coder explain this regex' → app:claude-cli). max_rows <= 0 still returns one row.

Alias targets are split with partition(':'), so a target written 'app:claude-cli' (cid 'app') never matches, and gateway model names containing ':' (common with ollama-style names) can't be alias targets.

command_for replaces EVERY argv element equal to a 'requires' program name, not only the program position. A prompt that is exactly 'claude', or a model named 'ptyxis', is rewritten to '/usr/bin/claude' (verified).

@matching lowercases the query but not app ids, gateway base ids or app model names, so uppercase ids and models are unreachable except through the display name. [aliases] keys are exact-match only: '@cl' does not reach alias 'cli'.

chat_url never receives {effort}, so a chat_url containing '{effort}' raises KeyError on activation. URL templates go through full str.format, so any literal '{' or '}' (for example JSON in a URL) breaks activation.

fill() rewrites literal template query parts: '/' → %2F (the documented 'folder=/home/you/...' example becomes folder=%2Fhome%2F...), '+' → %20, invalid %XX → %EF%BF%BD or %25XX, and key-only params ('?flag') disappear. It also drops '//' from 'scheme://?q=' URLs ('x:?q=...'), and lowercases the scheme only when a query exists.

Regex patterns are validated nowhere. They compile lazily at search time, so one bad pattern makes all rows disappear (D-Bus error; the prompt box list gets cleared), and the short-circuit means it may fail only for some prompts. The Rust port should validate at load and in the settings window's whole-config validation.

There is no schema or type validation. A string where a list is expected iterates its characters (patterns) or does substring matching (tags). An unknown key in [[app]] or [[routing.rule]] makes the whole config load fail with TypeError, so the provider service can't start, or every search returns an error. NaN priority breaks the sort. enabled = "false" (a string) counts as true.

The TOML editor writes strings with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True). Any value containing an astral character (emoji) becomes surrogate escapes that TOML rejects, so saving fails with EditError. Non-ASCII BMP text is stored as \uXXXX escapes instead of readable UTF-8.
The line-based editor splits with str.splitlines. A literal U+2028, U+0085 or \x0b-\x0c inside a string makes every edit fail. Any edit converts CRLF to LF and adds a final newline.

The HEADER regex has no awareness of multi-line arrays or strings: a last-element line like '["--verbose"]' on its own line, or '[search]' inside a """ string, counts as a table header. The readback check turns this into a safe but spurious EditError. Quoted or dotted table names and keys are not recognized either, and produce duplicate-table or duplicate-key errors.

Placement of missing keys: they are inserted right below the table header, above existing comments and keys. Several missing keys added to a new table come out in reverse order (chat_url above url, in both the editor and the legacy migration).
update() replaces a symlinked agents.toml with a regular file (verified), which breaks dotfile-managed configs. It has no fsync, a fixed temp file name, and does not preserve ownership.

set_secret is not atomic: it truncates, then writes. A pre-existing 0644 file holds the new key at 0644 until the chmod. It moves the key line to the end, creates a file containing only '\n' when removing a key from a missing file, and does not reject newlines in the value (line injection). read_env_file does not catch UnicodeDecodeError, so a non-UTF-8 secrets.env breaks the whole config load. Quote stripping is unpaired, and 'export KEY=' is not supported.

Legacy migration: an invalid settings.toml makes load() raise on every start. Array values or unknown app ids abort the migration silently, and it is then retried (and fails) on every load. Legacy app keys other than enabled, priority and cwd are dropped silently.
restore_defaults writes idle_minutes = 30.0 (float), while the settings window writes 30 (int), so the file flips between the two styles. Restore also always rewrites the file the first time.

Gateway: the cache timestamps start at 0.0 on the monotonic clock, so no fetch happens during the first 60 s after boot. A non-dict JSON body or entry, or IncompleteRead, escapes the except clause and fails the search. The fetch blocks the D-Bus handler and the GTK main thread for up to about 0.5 s per socket operation, without bounding DNS. display_name: null gives a row titled None. An entry whose base equals auto_model adds its efforts to the Auto row.

signature() covers only agents.toml and secrets.env, while CONFIGURATION.md says 'any of the three files'. Same-size edits within one timestamp tick are missed. PermissionError from stat is not caught.
parse_result_id breaks silently if an app id, gateway base or model contains '|'.

Launch: an empty argv after optional groups are dropped raises IndexError. A missing or empty cwd gives a FileNotFoundError, or the process cwd '.'. Children are never explicitly reaped, so the Rust resident prompt box must reap them. The clipboard helpers ignore EXTRA_PATH and wl-copy runs synchronously.
which() with PATH unset searches the process cwd first, because the leading empty PATH entry is honored.
Settings folder picker: '/home/jem2/x' becomes '~2/x', because the home-prefix test is a plain startswith. The gateway Test button fetches synchronously on the UI thread.
Dead code or inconsistencies: Query.is_empty, state_dir() and App.description are unused. activate() ignores enabled, so a disabled app's id still launches if one is passed in.

Test coverage gaps worth porting as new tests: Gateway HTTP and cache timing, read_env_file parsing, the activate()/copy_prompt paths, fill() normalization edge cases, the resolve() ordering edge cases (alias falling through, step 3 before step 4), max_rows <= 1, the toml_edit insertion position for missing keys, format_value float and str output, and line-ending normalization.

Next feature (full settings window): the current editor can only replace single-line scalars. It cannot write arrays (tags, models, efforts, requires, patterns), nested command lists or inline tables, add, delete or rename [[app]] blocks, edit [[routing.rule]] (no id), or delete keys. A toml_edit-crate (Rust) implementation will have different decor and placement rules, so keep the observable contract: an edited value keeps its key's indentation, separator and trailing comment. Then decide explicitly whether new keys go below the header (today) or at the end of the table (the toml_edit default).

specUi.area: Agent Search 0.5.0 user-facing surface: the SearchProvider2 D-Bus service, prompt box, settings window, GNOME shortcut module, and the bash installer/CLI with its templates. This is the behavior a Rust port (gtk4-rs + libadwaita-rs) must match. The ranker, launch and TOML-edit internals are included only where they decide what crosses D-Bus or gets written to disk.

behaviors.behavior: The provider process is a GApplication with application_id 'io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider', flags IS_SERVICE and inactivity_timeout 60000 ms. It only starts through D-Bus activation (the rendered .service Exec line, no extra args) and calls run(argv).
behaviors.edge_cases: If the bus name is already owned, registration fails and the process exits. GLib's own short startup grace for a service that has no calls yet is internal to GLib. A port built on gio::Application keeps it automatically; one built on zbus must re-create the startup grace and the idle exit itself.

behaviors.behavior: The constructor runs before bus registration. It loads config through config.load(): $LLM_SEARCH_HOME/config (default ~/.llm-search/config), agents.toml plus secrets.env. It then builds a fresh Gateway and records signature(). load() first runs migrate_legacy_settings, so a provider start can rewrite agents.toml and rename settings.toml to settings.toml.migrated.
behaviors.edge_cases: These all raise before run(), so the process dies: a TOML syntax error, an unknown key in an [[app]] or [[routing.rule]] table, or a missing id/name/tag/patterns. GNOME then gets no rows, and every new search re-triggers activation. A missing agents.toml gives the defaults (no apps). Unknown top-level tables and unknown keys in [search]/[gateway]/[prompt]/[routing] are ignored.

behaviors.behavior: In the dbus_register vfunc, the provider registers one object implementing org.gnome.Shell.SearchProvider2 with this exact signature set: GetInitialResultSet(as terms)->(as results); GetSubsearchResultSet(as previous_results, as terms)->(as results); GetResultMetas(as identifiers)->(aa{sv} metas); ActivateResult(s identifier, as terms, u timestamp)->(); LaunchSearch(as terms, u timestamp)->(). It registers at the object path GApplication passes in, which is derived from the app id: /io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch/SearchProvider. It then chains up. dbus_unregister unregisters the object. GApplication's own org.gtk.Application, org.freedesktop.Application and org.gtk.Actions are also exported at that path.
behaviors.edge_cases: The path must equal ObjectPath in the .ini. If the Rust app id changes, the derived path changes too.

behaviors.behavior: Every method call does hold() first and release() in a finally block. The 60 s inactivity timer therefore restarts after each reply, and the process exits 60 s after the last call. Calls run synchronously on the main loop, one at a time.
behaviors.edge_cases: A gateway fetch (up to 0.5 s) blocks every other call. An error reply still releases.

behaviors.behavior: GetInitialResultSet runs these steps in order. (1) reload_if_changed(). (2) q = query.parse(terms): the first '@x' term (length >1) becomes model, lowercased. The first '!alias' term whose alias is in EFFORT_ALIASES becomes effort. All other terms, joined by single spaces and stripped, form the prompt. (3) rows = ranker.rank(q, gateway.models() + app candidates, config), where app candidates are enabled apps whose 'requires' all resolve. (4) Store self.prompt = q.prompt and self.rows = {result_id: row} in rank order. (5) Return the ids in rank order.
behaviors.edge_cases: It returns [] when len(prompt) < min_chars, which includes token-only queries. Runs of spaces in the original query are lost. An invalid routing regex or a wrongly typed config value raises, giving a D-Bus Failed error rather than [].
behaviors.covered_by_test: ParseTests.test_cases, RankTests.* (ranking only, not the D-Bus layer)

behaviors.behavior: GetSubsearchResultSet ignores previous_results completely. It runs exactly the same full search as GetInitialResultSet on args[1] (the new terms), including the reload check and the gateway fetch.
behaviors.edge_cases: Results can contain ids that were not in previous_results.

behaviors.behavior: reload_if_changed runs before searches only. It compares signature() with the stored value; signature() is ((st_mtime_ns, st_size) or None for agents.toml, the same for secrets.env) in config_dir(). If they differ, it reloads the config, creates a new Gateway (which drops the 60 s model cache) and stores the new signature.
behaviors.edge_cases: If the reload raises, self.config keeps the old object but the signature is not updated. Every later search retries and fails with D-Bus Failed; there is no fallback to the last good config. A rewrite with the same size inside one mtime tick goes unnoticed. GetResultMetas and ActivateResult never reload.

behaviors.behavior: GetResultMetas walks the requested ids in order and silently skips any id that is not in the last search's rows. Each meta is an a{sv} with exactly four string ('s') keys. 'id': the id. 'name': row.title, i.e. candidate.name, plus ' · ' + model.capitalize() when a model was resolved (e.g. 'Agent · Opus'). 'description': '“' + last search prompt + '”', plus ' · ' + subtitle when the subtitle is non-empty. The subtitle is ['<effort> effort' if effort] + [', '.join(matched rule tags the candidate carries, in rule order)], joined by ' · '. 'gicon': g_icon_to_string(g_themed_icon_new(icon)).
behaviors.edge_cases: 'gicon' is the bare icon name, except that a name starting with '.' becomes '. GThemedIcon .x .x-symbolic'. Every meta uses the latest search's prompt. Ids from older searches are dropped because their query hash differs. The provider does no markup escaping (the Shell escapes). Default icons: apps 'system-search-symbolic', gateway models model_info.icon or 'user-available-symbolic', Auto 'emblem-system-symbolic'. There are no clipboardText or icon keys.

behaviors.behavior: Result id = '<cid>|<model or empty>|<effort or empty>|<qk>'. cid is one of 'app:<id>', 'model:<base>', 'auto'. qk is the lowercase hex of BLAKE2s with digest_size=6 (12 hex chars) over the UTF-8 bytes of model + '\0' + effort + '\0' + prompt. Ids must change whenever the query changes (GNOME caches metas by id) and be stable for the same query and unique within one search. parse_result_id splits on '|' and keeps the first 3 fields; empty fields become None.
behaviors.edge_cases: A '|' inside an app id breaks parsing; ids are not validated. The hash need not match the Python bytes exactly, but Blake2s with a 6-byte output is not truncated Blake2s-256; use blake2::Blake2sVar::new(6) if bit parity is wanted.

behaviors.behavior: ActivateResult re-parses the prompt from the terms argument (parse(terms).prompt), not from the stored prompt, then calls launch.activate. activate parses the id and finds the [[app]] whose 'app:<id>' equals cid. If copy_prompt is set, it copies the prompt with `wl-copy -- <prompt>`, or failing that `xclip -selection clipboard` on stdin. If command is non-empty, it builds argv = fill_command (an item is dropped when its placeholder is empty; a nested list is dropped whole if any placeholder in it is empty) and replaces 'requires' program names with absolute which() paths. It spawns with no shell, start_new_session, stdin/stdout/stderr on /dev/null, cwd = expanduser(cwd) and the inherited env, logs 'running <argv0> in <cwd>' and returns. Otherwise it fills the URL from the app url, or for model/auto from the gateway chat_url, with URL-encoded values and empty query params dropped. It opens the URL with Gio.AppInfo.launch_default_for_uri(url, None) and logs 'opening <url before ?>'. The timestamp is ignored and the reply is empty.
behaviors.edge_cases: An unknown id, an empty url, or an empty chat_url is a silent success. These raise D-Bus Failed: missing cwd, no URI handler, an unknown {placeholder} (str.format KeyError). No launch context or activation token is passed. It uses the config from the last search. Children inherit the service env, which today includes PYTHONPATH and LLM_SEARCH_HOME.

behaviors.behavior: LaunchSearch is fire-and-forget. On the session bus it calls dest 'io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch', path '/io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch', interface org.freedesktop.Application, method ActivateAction with body ('search', [<' '.join(terms)>], {}) of type (sava{sv}). Flags are NONE, so auto-start is allowed, and the timeout is the default. No reply handler is attached and the method returns an empty reply at once. The raw terms, including @model and !effort tokens, are joined with single spaces, so the prompt box shows the whole query.
behaviors.edge_cases: Errors are silently lost, e.g. when the prompt box is not installed. The timestamp is dropped and platform_data is empty (no activation-token), so focus-stealing prevention may apply.

behaviors.behavior: An unknown method returns org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownMethod with the method name as the message. Any exception in a handler is logged with log.exception('%s failed', method), which includes a traceback, and returns org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed with str(e). The service never exits because of one bad query.
behaviors.edge_cases: In Rust, handlers must not panic: catch_unwind, or map every Result to a Failed error.

behaviors.behavior: Logging uses logging.basicConfig(level=INFO, format='%(name)s: %(message)s') to stderr, with logger name 'llm-search'. Journal lines therefore start with 'llm-search: '. Each launch writes one INFO line containing argv[0] and cwd, or the URL without its query string; the prompt is never logged.
behaviors.edge_cases: The docs tell users to run journalctl --user -b | grep -i -E 'llm-search|LlmSearchProvider', so keep the prefix.

behaviors.behavior: Gateway.models() returns [] when no url is set. Otherwise it returns the cached list for 60 s after a success and [] for 30 s after a failure. A fetch is GET <url, trailing '/' removed at load>/model/info, with 'Authorization: Bearer <secrets[key_env]>' when that secret is non-empty, timeout 0.5 s, response parsed as JSON .data. On OSError or ValueError it returns [] and starts the back-off. Gateway models come before apps in the candidate order.
behaviors.edge_cases: Non-object JSON or entries that are not dicts raise AttributeError, which is not caught, so the search returns Failed. The fetch blocks the main loop.

behaviors.behavior: The prompt box is an Adw.Application with application_id 'io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch' and flags DEFAULT_FLAGS: a single instance, and later launches forward to the primary. It is normally D-Bus-activated through the rendered service with --gapplication-service, in which case GApplication waits for Activate/ActivateAction and does not activate on startup. Its Wayland app_id is the app id, which matches the .desktop id.
behaviors.edge_cases: The Rust binary must accept --gapplication-service, which gio::Application handles when IS_SERVICE/IS_LAUNCHER are not set.

behaviors.behavior: The constructor loads config (including the legacy migration), creates a Gateway, stores signature(), sets window and settings to None and the idle source to 0, and registers the actions.
behaviors.edge_cases: A config load error kills the app before it registers.

behaviors.behavior: Two actions are registered. 'search' takes parameter type 's' and calls open(text); text may be '', which clears the entry. 'preferences' takes no parameter and calls open_settings(). Both can be reached through org.freedesktop.Application.ActivateAction, org.gtk.Actions and `gapplication action`.
behaviors.edge_cases: The app has no HANDLES_OPEN, so Open() is unsupported.

behaviors.behavior: startup chains up, loads the CSS (PB-18) from a string into a Gtk.CssProvider, and adds it for the default display at STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_APPLICATION. It then calls self.hold() once. That hold is never released, so the app only exits through quit().
behaviors.edge_cases: The CSS also applies to the settings window.

behaviors.behavior: activate calls open(None), which keeps the previous entry text.
behaviors.edge_cases: After Esc, the box reopens with the old text; after a send, the text was cleared.

behaviors.behavior: open(text): cancel the idle timer; if config.signature() differs from the stored one, reload (config, new Gateway, signature); create the PromptWindow once, lazily, and reuse it for the life of the process; then summon(text).
behaviors.edge_cases: Config changes are picked up only when the box opens or when the settings window saves, not on each keystroke.

behaviors.behavior: summon(text): if text is not None, entry.set_text(text), which also triggers refresh; then refresh(), present(), entry.grab_focus(), and entry.set_position(-1), leaving the cursor at the end with nothing selected.
behaviors.edge_cases: refresh runs twice when text is given.

behaviors.behavior: The window is an Adw.ApplicationWindow: title 'Agent Search', resizable False, default size 680 x -1 (height follows content), hide_on_close True, no header bar. Its content is a vertical Gtk.Box (spacing 10, class 'prompt-box') holding three children. (1) A horizontal Box (spacing 6) with a Gtk.Entry: hexpand, class 'prompt-entry', placeholder 'Ask anything…  @model to choose · !high for effort' (two spaces after the U+2026 ellipsis, U+00B7 middle dots), primary icon 'system-search-symbolic'. Next to it a gear Gtk.Button: icon 'emblem-system-symbolic', tooltip 'Settings (Ctrl+,)', valign CENTER, classes 'flat' and 'circular', calling open_settings. (2) A Gtk.ListBox with selection BROWSE and classes 'boxed-list' and 'prompt-rows'. (3) A Gtk.Label 'Enter to send · ↑↓ to choose · Esc to close · Ctrl+, for settings' with classes 'dim-label' and 'caption', margin_top 4.
behaviors.edge_cases: The window is created once and hidden, never destroyed. Alt+F4 hides it, which triggers PB-10.

behaviors.behavior: A window key controller in CAPTURE phase handles four cases. Escape (any modifiers) calls dismiss(). keyval 'comma' with CONTROL_MASK in state (other modifiers not excluded) calls open_settings(). Down or Tab (any modifiers) calls move(+1). Up or ISO_Left_Tab calls move(-1). These keys are consumed and never reach the entry. All other keys propagate, so Enter and KP_Enter reach the entry's 'activate'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Tab never moves focus, so the gear cannot be reached by keyboard. Ctrl+Tab also moves the selection.

behaviors.behavior: Focus-out dismiss: on notify::is-active, if the window is not active, call dismiss(). This works like a spotlight: clicking elsewhere closes the box.
behaviors.edge_cases: Esc, a send or Alt+F4 call dismiss twice (harmless, because start_idle_timer cancels first). See bug note on the ordering with open_settings.

behaviors.behavior: refresh() runs on every entry 'changed'. It removes all rows, then computes q = parse(entry.get_text().split()) and rank(q, candidates(config, gateway), config). Each Row becomes an Adw.ActionRow: title = markup-escaped row.title, subtitle = markup-escaped row.subtitle, activatable, with a prefix Gtk.Image(icon_name=candidate.icon, pixel_size=32), and keeps result_id. The list and the hint are visible only when there are rows. The first row is selected.
behaviors.edge_cases: Unlike the Shell metas, rows do not show the quoted prompt. After the cache expires, a keystroke can block up to 0.5 s on the gateway. An exception (e.g. a bad regex) leaves the list empty.

behaviors.behavior: Sending: Enter (entry 'activate') runs the selected row, or does nothing if there are no rows. 'row-activated' (a single click in BROWSE mode) runs that row. run(row): prompt = parse(entry text split).prompt; launch.activate(config, row.result_id, prompt); entry.set_text(''); dismiss().
behaviors.edge_cases: If activate raises, the entry is not cleared and the window stays open.

behaviors.behavior: move(step): index = (selected index, or -1) + step; target = row at max(0, index); select it if it exists. There is no wrap: Up at the top stays on row 0, and Down past the end stays put.
behaviors.edge_cases: With no rows it is a no-op.

behaviors.behavior: dismiss(): window.set_visible(False), then app.start_idle_timer().
behaviors.edge_cases: The entry text is kept.

behaviors.behavior: Resident and idle behavior. start_idle_timer first cancels any existing timer. If any window in app.get_windows() is visible, it starts no timer. Otherwise minutes = config.prompt_idle_minutes (default 30.0): if minutes <= 0, quit() immediately; else timeout_add_seconds(int(minutes*60)), and quit() when it fires. open() and open_settings() cancel the timer.
behaviors.edge_cases: int() truncates, so 0.01 minutes gives 0 s. Windows without an application (ShortcutDialog) do not count. If the process was D-Bus-started but no window was ever closed (e.g. by a bus introspection, or an action that failed), the timer is never armed and the process stays resident indefinitely.

behaviors.behavior: open_settings(): cancel the idle timer; hide the prompt window if visible; if there is no settings window or it is not visible, construct a new SettingsWindow; present() it and return it.
behaviors.edge_cases: Opening settings from the box hides the box, and the box does not come back when settings closes. A visible settings window is reused without being rebuilt.

behaviors.behavior: reload() reloads config, creates a new Gateway and updates the signature. The settings window calls it after every successful save.
behaviors.edge_cases: It raises on invalid TOML, and nothing catches it in the callers.

behaviors.behavior: The CSS text is exactly: '.prompt-box { padding: 12px; }', '.prompt-entry { font-size: 1.35em; min-height: 44px; }', '.prompt-rows row { padding: 6px 4px; }'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Requires GTK >= 4.12 (load_from_string).

behaviors.behavior: The settings window is an Adw.Window: application=app, title 'Agent Search Settings', default size 600x680. Its content is an Adw.ToolbarView whose top bar is an Adw.HeaderBar with title_widget = Adw.ViewSwitcher(stack, policy WIDE), and whose content is an Adw.ToastOverlay around an Adw.ViewStack.
behaviors.edge_cases: There is no bottom ViewSwitcherBar, so the layout is not adaptive. The minimum versions are libadwaita 1.5 (AlertDialog) and 1.4 (SpinRow, ToolbarView).

behaviors.behavior: build_pages() remembers the visible child name, removes every page, and adds three pages in this order: ('general', 'General', 'preferences-system-symbolic'), ('agents', 'Agents', 'system-users-symbolic'), ('gateway', 'Gateway', 'network-server-symbolic'). It then restores the visible page.
behaviors.edge_cases: A rebuild discards unsaved text in entry rows.

behaviors.behavior: A key controller in the default bubble phase closes the window on Escape, whatever the modifiers.
behaviors.edge_cases: Ctrl+, does nothing here.

behaviors.behavior: close-request: cancel the file monitor, schedule GLib.idle_add(app.start_idle_timer) to run once, and return False so the window is destroyed rather than hidden.
behaviors.edge_cases: A pending 300 ms refresh timer is not removed and may fire on the dead window.

behaviors.behavior: Live refresh: a Gio file monitor watches <dir>/agents.toml with flag WATCH_MOVES; any 'changed' event calls schedule_refresh(). That adds one 300 ms timeout if none is pending. refresh_from_disk() then checks whether signature(dir) differs from app.signature. Equal means the change came from our own save (because _write already reloaded), so nothing happens. Different means app.reload(), build_pages(), and the toast 'Updated from agents.toml'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Only agents.toml is watched, not secrets.env or gsettings. Atomic rename saves from editors fire the monitor (MOVED_IN/CREATED). Opening the prompt box also updates app.signature and can mask an external edit. Same-size edits inside one mtime tick are missed.

behaviors.behavior: Saving: save(section, key, v) and save_app(app_id, key, v) produce one edit tuple, (section, key, None, v) or ('app', key, app_id, v), and pass it to config.update(edits, dir). An EditError shows the toast 'Couldn't save: <msg>'. An OSError shows 'Couldn't save: <strerror>'. On success it calls app.reload(); there is no success toast.
behaviors.edge_cases: After a failed save the widget keeps showing the unsaved value; nothing reverts it. Other exceptions are not caught, e.g. UnicodeDecodeError, or a TOMLDecodeError in reload after an outside edit.

behaviors.behavior: toast(text) adds Adw.Toast(title=markup-escaped text, timeout=3).

spin_row(title, subtitle, value, lower, upper, step, cb, digits=0) uses Adw.SpinRow.new_with_range(lower, upper, step), then sets title, subtitle, digits and the value before connecting the handler, so building the row never saves. On every notify::value it calls cb(value if digits else int(value)), so each click or step rewrites agents.toml.
behaviors.edge_cases: An out-of-range value in the file is clamped in the display only and not saved. A fractional value in a digits=0 row is shown rounded and truncated on the next change.

behaviors.behavior: entry_row(title, text, cb, password=False) uses Adw.PasswordEntryRow or Adw.EntryRow with show_apply_button=True and set_text(text). The 'apply' signal calls cb(text.strip()). Nothing is saved while typing.
behaviors.edge_cases: The row keeps the unstripped text after apply.

behaviors.behavior: button_row(title, subtitle, label, cb, icon=None) is an Adw.ActionRow(title, subtitle) with a suffix Gtk.Button (valign CENTER, tooltip=label). With an icon, the button gets that icon name plus the 'flat' class; without one, it shows label as text. It is set as the row's activatable widget, so clicking the row clicks the button.
behaviors.edge_cases: Titles and subtitles are interpreted as markup.

behaviors.behavior: General page, group 'Prompt Box'. First, an ActionRow 'Keyboard Shortcut', subtitle 'Opens the prompt box from anywhere', with suffixes Gtk.ShortcutLabel(valign CENTER, disabled_text 'None') and Gtk.Button 'Change…' (valign CENTER), which presents ShortcutDialog. The label is filled from shortcut.get(); a GLib.Error gives ''. Second, a SpinRow 'Keep Running After Closing', subtitle 'Minutes; opens instantly within this time. 0 quits at once', value [prompt] idle_minutes, range 0..480, step 5, digits 0, saving ('prompt', 'idle_minutes', int).
behaviors.edge_cases: The shortcut row itself is not activatable.

behaviors.behavior: General page, group 'Results' (description 'Used by both the prompt box and GNOME search'), three int SpinRows. 'Minimum Characters' / 'Shorter prompts show no rows', range 1..20 step 1, saves ('search', 'min_chars'). 'Rows Shown' / 'GNOME search shows about five', range 1..10 step 1, saves ('search', 'max_rows'). 'Low Effort Up To' / 'Prompts with this many words or fewer get low effort', range 0..50 step 1, saves ('routing', 'low_effort_max_words').
behaviors.edge_cases: The file may hold 0 or values above the range; the rows clamp them.

behaviors.behavior: General page, group 'Configuration Files', three button rows. 'agents.toml' / 'Add agents, aliases and ranking rules. Every setting is explained in the file', label 'Open', icon 'document-edit-symbolic': opens the file:// URI of <dir>/agents.toml with launch_default_for_uri. 'Restore Defaults' / 'Puts the settings on this page back to factory values. Agents, rules, the gateway and the shortcut are kept', a text button 'Restore…' that opens the confirm dialog. 'Documentation' / 'Search syntax, providers and troubleshooting', label 'Open', icon 'help-browser-symbolic': opens https://github.com/oscillatingjem/gnome-llm-search-provider/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md.
behaviors.edge_cases: A missing URI handler raises an uncaught GLib.Error.
