behaviors.behavior: Restore uses an Adw.AlertDialog with heading 'Restore Defaults?' and body 'Minimum characters, rows shown, the low-effort limit and how long the box keeps running go back to factory values in agents.toml. Your agents, aliases, ranking rules, gateway and shortcut are kept.' Its responses are 'cancel'/'Cancel' and 'restore'/'Restore' (DESTRUCTIVE), with default response 'cancel', presented on the window. Only 'restore' acts. It calls config.restore_defaults(dir), which is a single update of [search] min_chars=3, [search] max_rows=5, [prompt] idle_minutes=30.0 (a float, written '30.0'), and [routing] low_effort_max_words=8. On error the toast is 'Couldn't restore defaults: <strerror or msg>'. On success: app.reload(), self.close(), then app.open_settings() builds a new window (General page) and toasts 'Defaults restored'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Missing tables are appended. Agents, aliases, rules, the gateway and the shortcut are untouched.

behaviors.behavior: Agents page. Group 'Agents', description 'Turn agents on or off, and change how they rank. Higher priority ranks higher.', has one row per [[app]] in file order, including disabled and not-installed apps. A separate untitled group holds the button row 'Add an Agent' / 'New agents are added in agents.toml, which has ready-made examples', label 'Open', icon 'list-add-symbolic', which opens agents.toml.
behaviors.edge_cases: There is no add, delete or rename in the UI yet; that is the planned next feature.

behaviors.behavior: Agent row subtitle, in order of precedence. If any 'requires' program fails launch.which (PATH + ~/.local/bin + ~/bin): 'Not installed: ' + ', '.join(missing). Else, if command is non-empty: 'Runs ' + (' '.join(top-level str items not containing '{'))[:60]. Else: 'Opens ' + url.split('?')[0].
behaviors.edge_cases: The 60-character cut applies to the joined string, counts code points and adds no ellipsis. Nested lists are skipped. An empty url gives 'Opens '.

behaviors.behavior: Each agent is an Adw.ExpanderRow: title and subtitle markup-escaped, show_enable_switch True, enable_expansion = app.enabled. notify::enable-expansion saves ('app', 'enabled', bool) for that id. Children: SpinRow 'Priority' / 'Added to its ranking score', range -10..10, step 0.5, digits 1, saving a float ('app', 'priority'). Only when command is non-empty: EntryRow 'Working Folder' (text = cwd) whose apply saves cwd = (value or '~'), with a suffix flat Button 'folder-open-symbolic' (tooltip 'Choose Folder') that opens the folder chooser. Then an ActionRow 'Good At' with subtitle '<', '.join(tags) or none> (edit in agents.toml)'.
behaviors.edge_cases: A disabled agent cannot be expanded, so its priority and cwd cannot be edited until it is switched on. URL agents have no cwd row.

behaviors.behavior: The folder chooser is a Gtk.FileDialog(title 'Working Folder for <name>') using select_folder(parent=window). A GLib.Error, including cancel, does nothing. Otherwise path = folder.get_path(); if it starts with GLib.get_home_dir() as a plain string prefix, it becomes '~' + rest. Then row.set_text(path) and save cwd.
behaviors.edge_cases: Because the prefix check has no separator, /home/jem2 becomes '~2'. get_path() can be None for a non-native folder.

behaviors.behavior: Gateway page. Group 'LiteLLM Gateway', description 'Optional. Connect a LiteLLM proxy to list API models (OpenAI, Anthropic API, LM Studio, Ollama…) as rows. Leave the URL empty to turn it off.' It holds these rows. EntryRow 'Gateway URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4000)' (text = url with trailing '/' stripped) saves ('gateway', 'url'). EntryRow 'Chat URL ({model} and {prompt} are filled in)' saves ('gateway', 'chat_url'). EntryRow 'Auto Model' saves ('gateway', 'auto_model'). PasswordEntryRow 'Gateway Key (saved to secrets.env as <key_env>)' (text = the current secret) calls save_key. Button row 'Connection' / 'Not tested' / 'Test' runs the test. A second group holds 'Setup Guide' / 'Running LiteLLM and a chat UI, and adding providers', label 'Open', icon 'help-browser-symbolic', opening docs/PROVIDERS.md on GitHub.
behaviors.edge_cases: Saving an empty value writes ''. A missing [gateway] table is appended. key_env is not editable in the UI.

behaviors.behavior: save_key(v) calls config.set_secret(key_env, v, dir). set_secret drops every line whose strip().partition('=')[0].strip() equals the key (comment lines are kept), appends 'KEY=value' if v is non-empty, and writes '\n'.join(lines) + '\n' via os.open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o600), followed by chmod 600. OSError shows the toast 'Couldn't save the key: <strerror>'. On success: app.reload() and the toast 'Key saved', or 'Key removed' when v is empty.
behaviors.edge_cases: The write is not atomic. The value is written raw, unquoted. On read, read_env_file strips surrounding quotes and whitespace, so a key that starts or ends with ' or " is mangled.

behaviors.behavior: The test uses the saved config only. With an empty url the subtitle becomes 'No gateway URL set'. Otherwise it runs a fresh Gateway(c).models() synchronously (no cache). If models came back: 'Connected: <n> models (<first 4 names, ', '><'…' if n>4>)'. If not: 'Couldn't reach <url>, or it lists no models'. Subtitles are markup-escaped.
behaviors.edge_cases: A typed but unapplied URL is not tested. The Auto model counts toward n. The UI freezes for up to 0.5 s. Non-dict JSON raises uncaught.

behaviors.behavior: ShortcutDialog is an Adw.Window: transient_for the settings window, modal, title 'Set Shortcut', resizable False, default 420 x -1, and no application. Its content is a ToolbarView with an Adw.HeaderBar on top and an Adw.StatusPage (icon 'input-keyboard-symbolic', title 'Press the New Shortcut', description 'Esc to cancel · Backspace to remove the shortcut', class 'compact'). It has a key controller in CAPTURE phase.
behaviors.edge_cases: It does not count toward the idle check.

behaviors.behavior: Capture rules, with mods = state & Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask(). Escape with no mods closes the dialog. BackSpace with no mods calls set_shortcut('') (removes the shortcut) and closes. A keyval in MODIFIER_KEYS (Shift_L/R, Control_L/R, Alt_L/R, Super_L/R, Meta_L/R, Hyper_L/R, ISO_Level3_Shift, Caps_Lock) is consumed while the dialog keeps waiting. Any other key with no mods is consumed and ignored. Anything else calls set_shortcut(Gtk.accelerator_name(Gdk.keyval_to_lower(keyval), mods)) and closes. Every key is consumed.
behaviors.edge_cases: On GTK 4.22, accelerator_name gives '<Control><Super>space' (not '<Primary>'). Shift+letter is accepted as '<Shift>a'. Plain F-keys and media keys are rejected. There is no conflict check.

behaviors.behavior: set_shortcut(b) calls shortcut.set(b). RuntimeError or GLib.Error shows the toast 'Couldn't set the shortcut: <e>'. It always finishes with refresh_shortcut(), which sets the label from shortcut.get().

On-disk edits through config.update and toml_edit.apply. The file is read (missing gives ''). Each edit is applied to the text. If the text is unchanged, nothing is written. Otherwise the new text goes to '<dir>/.agents.toml.tmp', which gets the existing file's permission bits, and is renamed over agents.toml. For a [table] key: the first line matching ^\s*key\s*=\s* inside that table's span (up to the next header) has only its value replaced; the indent, the original '=' spacing and the trailing whitespace and comment are kept. A missing key is inserted on the line right after the header. A missing table is appended as '', '[table]  # added by the settings window', 'key = value'. For [[app]] by id: the block whose 'id = ' value equals the id is used, and a missing key goes right after the id line. Value formatting: bools 'true'/'false'; ints and floats via Python repr ('2.5', '30.0'); strings via json.dumps. When it fails, the file is left untouched: an unknown id raises EditError "no [[app]] with id '<id>'"; a multi-line existing value raises '<key> is a multi-line value; edit it in the file'; after all edits the result is parsed and every value read back, and a parse failure raises 'the edit would break the file: <msg>' while a mismatch raises '<table>.<key> reads back as <got!r>, not <value!r>'. Lines are joined with '\n' plus a final '\n'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Comments and untouched lines must stay byte-identical. With toml_edit in Rust, copy the old value's decor (suffix comment) onto the new value, and insert missing keys after the header or id line, not at the end of the table.

behaviors.behavior: Schemas: 'org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys' (key 'custom-keybindings', type as) and the relocatable 'org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys.custom-keybinding' (keys name, command, binding) at path '/org/gnome/settings-daemon/plugins/media-keys/custom-keybindings/llm-search/'. 'Available' means both schemas are found by a recursive lookup in the default SettingsSchemaSource.
behaviors.edge_cases: Check availability first: Gio.Settings.new on a missing schema aborts the process.

behaviors.behavior: get() returns '' when the schemas are unavailable or the path is not in custom-keybindings. Otherwise it returns the 'binding' string at the path, e.g. '<Primary><Super>space'.
behaviors.edge_cases: The binding is returned as stored, even if it does not parse.

behaviors.behavior: set(binding) with a non-empty binding sets name = 'Agent Search' (always), command = '<$HOME>/.local/bin/llm-search prompt' (absolute, no tilde) and binding = binding. Only after that does it append the path to the end of custom-keybindings, if it is not there yet.
behaviors.edge_cases: This name differs from the installer, which uses --name. When the schemas are unavailable it raises RuntimeError("GNOME's keyboard settings schemas aren't installed").

behaviors.behavior: set('') removes the path from custom-keybindings, keeping the order of the other entries, and resets name, command and binding at the path.
behaviors.edge_cases: In Rust, call gio::Settings::sync() before quit() so the dconf writes are not lost when idle_minutes = 0.

behaviors.behavior: Dispatch: no argument or 'help', '-h', '--help' prints the usage (exit 0). 'install', 'uninstall', 'status' (extra args ignored), 'query', 'test', and 'prompt' or its undocumented alias 'open' run their commands. Anything else prints the usage and exits 2. The script runs with set -euo pipefail. warn prints 'warning: <m>' to stderr; die prints 'error: <m>' to stderr and exits 1.

Paths: ROOT is the parent of the real (readlink -f) script directory. LLM_SEARCH_HOME=${LLM_SEARCH_HOME:-$HOME/.llm-search}; DATA_HOME=${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}; BIN_HOME=$HOME/.local/bin (XDG_BIN_HOME is not honored); COPY_DIR=$DATA_HOME/llm-search; RENDER_DIR=$LLM_SEARCH_HOME/state/install; XDG_DIR=$LLM_SEARCH_HOME/state/xdg; ENVD_FILE=${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/environment.d/60-llm-search.conf; ENVD_GENERATOR=/usr/lib/systemd/user-environment-generators/30-systemd-environment-d-generator.

Usage text exactly as in the heredoc. It lists install [--copy] [--dry-run] [--name NAME] [--shortcut BINDING] with the descriptions of --copy, --name and --shortcut; uninstall [--purge] [--dry-run]; status; query WORDS...; prompt [TEXT...]; test; and the line 'Config home: $LLM_SEARCH_HOME (currently <path>)'.
behaviors.edge_cases: The 'open' alias and the '--category-name' option are not documented.

behaviors.behavior: install option parsing: --copy; --dry-run; --name or --category-name NAME (default 'Agent Search'); --shortcut BINDING. A missing or empty value hits bash ${2:?} and exits 1. An unknown option gives 'error: unknown option for install: <opt>'. Then, if LLM_SEARCH_HOME or ROOT contains a space: 'error: paths with spaces are not supported'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Spaces in HOME, DATA_HOME or COPY_DIR are not checked.

behaviors.behavior: Requirement checks. find_python takes the first of $PYTHON, /usr/bin/python3 and `command -v python3` that is executable and >= 3.11; none found: warning 'Python 3.11 or newer is required', then exit 1. If Gio cannot be imported: 'PyGObject (Gio) is missing. Install it with: <hint>', then exit 1. The hint comes from /etc/os-release ID/ID_LIKE: fedora|rhel 'sudo dnf install python3-gobject'; debian|ubuntu 'sudo apt install python3-gi gir1.2-glib-2.0'; arch 'sudo pacman -S python-gobject'; suse|opensuse 'sudo zypper install python3-gobject'; otherwise a generic line. Non-fatal: 'GNOME Shell not found; the provider only works in GNOME'; 'xdg-open not found (package xdg-utils)'; and the stdout line 'note: install wl-clipboard to enable the copy-prompt option' when neither wl-copy nor xclip exists.
behaviors.edge_cases: GTK 4 and libadwaita typelibs are not checked. For Rust this becomes a check of the binary and the runtime libraries.

behaviors.behavior: install prints 'Installing llm-search' and '  config home: <home>'. With --copy, CODE_ROOT=COPY_DIR: it prints '  copying code to <dir>', runs mkdir -p and cp -r ROOT/{bin,src,share,examples} into it (overlay, nothing deleted). Without it, CODE_ROOT=ROOT and it prints '  code runs from <ROOT>'. CODE_ROOT feeds @SRC@ and the ~/.local/bin/llm-search link. Templates and examples are always read from $ROOT.

Config seeding: mkdir -p config, state and state/install. For each file in ROOT/examples/config/* (agents.toml, and secrets.env.example installed as secrets.env): if it exists, print '  keeping existing config/<name>'; else print '  creating config/<name>' and copy it. Then chmod 600 config/secrets.env, every time.
behaviors.edge_cases: A user's file is never overwritten. The new file is briefly mode 644 before the chmod.

behaviors.behavior: Legacy cleanup (remove_old_install, run by both install and uninstall), for the old app id io.github.oscillatingjem.LlmSearchProvider. If any of these is a symlink it is removed with the message '  removed old <path>': $XDG_DIR/gnome-shell/search-providers/OLD.search-provider.ini, $DATA_HOME/gnome-shell/search-providers/OLD.search-provider.ini, $DATA_HOME/dbus-1/services/OLD.service, $DATA_HOME/applications/OLD.desktop, $DATA_HOME/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/OLD.svg. Then rm -f $RENDER_DIR/OLD.*.
behaviors.edge_cases: Regular files are left alone.

behaviors.behavior: Rendering: sed globally replaces @SRC@ with $CODE_ROOT/src, @HOME@ with $LLM_SEARCH_HOME, @PYTHON@ with $PY, @BIN@ with $BIN_HOME/llm-search, and @CATEGORY@ with the --name value. Outputs in RENDER_DIR: io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider.service, io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.service, io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.desktop. The .search-provider.ini and .svg are copied verbatim. Everything is re-rendered on every install. A dry run prints '  would render <basename>'.
behaviors.edge_cases: The sed replacement is not escaped (see bugs). In Rust, @SRC@ and @PYTHON@ go away; @HOME@, @BIN@ and @CATEGORY@ stay.

behaviors.behavior: Symlinks (target -> source). The same list drives install, uninstall and status: $XDG_DIR/gnome-shell/search-providers/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.search-provider.ini -> $RENDER_DIR/<same>; $DATA_HOME/dbus-1/services/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider.service -> $RENDER_DIR/<same>; $DATA_HOME/dbus-1/services/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.service -> $RENDER_DIR/<same>; $DATA_HOME/applications/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.desktop -> $RENDER_DIR/<same>; $DATA_HOME/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.svg -> $RENDER_DIR/<same>; $HOME/.local/bin/llm-search -> $CODE_ROOT/bin/llm-search. For each: mkdir -p the parent; if the target exists and is not a symlink, warn '<target> exists and is not a symlink; leaving it alone' and skip it; otherwise ln -sfn and print '  linked <target>'.
behaviors.edge_cases: A dangling symlink is replaced. The ini file name uses APP_ID, not PROVIDER_ID.

behaviors.behavior: environment.d: the line is 'XDG_DATA_DIRS=<XDG_DIR expanded>:${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share/:/usr/share/}', where the ${...} part stays literal for systemd. If ENVD_FILE has that exact full line, print '  keeping <file>'. Otherwise print '  writing <file>', mkdir -p, and overwrite the file with '# Added by llm-search: lets GNOME Shell find its search provider.\n<line>\n'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Any other content in the file is lost on rewrite. A Rust installer must recognise this exact line so existing installs print 'keeping'.

behaviors.behavior: environment.d safety check. It is skipped in dry runs and when the generator is not executable. Otherwise the installer runs ENVD_GENERATOR with stderr discarded and extracts the XDG_DATA_DIRS= value. If ':<dirs>:' lacks ':<XDG_DIR>:' or lacks ':/usr/share/:', it runs rm -f ENVD_FILE and dies with "environment.d check failed (XDG_DATA_DIRS would be '<dirs>'); removed <file>" (exit 1). By then the links already exist; the shortcut and restart steps have not run.
behaviors.edge_cases: The generator expands variables against the installer's own environment, not a clean login.

behaviors.behavior: 0.1.0 legacy cleanup: if $DATA_HOME/gnome-shell/search-providers/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.search-provider.ini is a symlink, remove it and print '  removed unused <path>'.

install_shortcut runs only with --shortcut. Without gsettings it warns 'gsettings not found; skipping the shortcut' and returns 0. It reads list = `gsettings get org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys custom-keybindings`. If the list does not contain the path: '@as []' or '[]' becomes "['<path>']", otherwise ", '<path>'" is inserted before the final ']'; then gsettings set. Next, on '<schema>:<path>' it sets name '<--name>', command '$HOME/.local/bin/llm-search prompt' and binding '<BINDING verbatim>'. It prints '  shortcut <b> opens the prompt box (change it in Settings > Keyboard > Custom Shortcuts)'.
behaviors.edge_cases: The list is updated before the keys, the opposite order to shortcut.py. The binding is not validated. Without --shortcut, an existing shortcut is left untouched.

behaviors.behavior: Restart and refresh: `pkill -f -- "-m llm_searc[h]" || true` kills the running Python provider and prompt box so the new code and config load. Then, if update-desktop-database exists, `update-desktop-database -q $DATA_HOME/applications`.
behaviors.edge_cases: After the migration this must kill both the legacy Python processes and the Rust binaries. Otherwise an old process keeps owning the bus name until idle (60 s for the provider, up to 30 min for the box).

behaviors.behavior: The final message is 'Done. Next steps:' followed by four steps. (1) Log out and back in. (2) 'Settings → Search: turn on "<name>"…'. (3) With a shortcut: 'Open the prompt box with <b>, or from the app grid ("<name>").'; without one, the app-grid line plus "./install.sh --shortcut '<Primary><Super>space'". (4) 'Edit <home>/config/agents.toml …'. Last, '  note: <BIN_HOME> is not on your PATH' when it is not.

uninstall takes --purge and --dry-run; an unknown option gives 'error: unknown option for uninstall: <opt>'. Every link target that is a symlink (wherever it points) is removed with '  removed <target>'. Then remove_old_install and remove_shortcut. If ENVD_FILE exists and contains 'llm-search' anywhere, it is removed with '  removed <file>'. Then the same pkill as install. With --purge: rm -rf $LLM_SEARCH_HOME $COPY_DIR and '  removed <home>'. Without it: rm -rf $RENDER_DIR and '  kept your config in <home> (use --purge to remove it)'. Last: 'Log out and back in to remove the category from search.'
behaviors.edge_cases: Without --purge, COPY_DIR and the empty state/xdg stay behind. update-desktop-database is not run.

behaviors.behavior: remove_shortcut: without gsettings, or when the list does not contain the path, it returns. Otherwise it computes the new list with `python3 -I` (ast.literal_eval of the list after stripping '@as ', path filtered out, printed as a Python list repr) and runs gsettings set. Then `gsettings reset-recursively <schema>:<path>` and '  removed the keyboard shortcut'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Needs python3 on PATH, which a Rust port must drop.

behaviors.behavior: status prints 'config home: <home>'. For each link it prints '  ok      <target>' if it is a symlink, else '  missing <target>'. For the provider ('search provider') and the app ('prompt box') it checks org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner through gdbus and prints '<label>: running' or '<label>: not running (starts when needed)'. Last it prints 'shortcut: <gsettings get binding output, quotes included>' or 'shortcut: none'.
behaviors.edge_cases: A dangling link counts as ok. environment.d and XDG_DATA_DIRS are not checked.

behaviors.behavior: test runs `<python> -m unittest discover -s $ROOT/tests "$@"`. Without Python 3.11 it fails with 'error: Python 3.11+ not found'.
behaviors.edge_cases: The comments in users' agents.toml tell them to run `llm-search test`, so keep the subcommand (e.g. as a config check).

behaviors.behavior: query WORDS runs gdbus call --session --dest io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider --object-path /io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch/SearchProvider --method org.gnome.Shell.SearchProvider2.GetInitialResultSet "['w1','w2',…]". It prints gdbus's output, e.g. "(['app:claude-chat||low|<hash>', …],)", and exits with gdbus's status.
behaviors.edge_cases: Words are not quote-escaped. With no words it sends [''].

behaviors.behavior: prompt/open [TEXT...]. When gapplication is available: with TEXT, it execs `gapplication action io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch search <GVariant text of ' '.join(TEXT)>`, the text produced by GLib.Variant('s',…).print_(False); without TEXT, it execs `gapplication launch io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch`. gapplication forwards DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID and XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN from the env as platform data. Without gapplication it runs PYTHONPATH=$ROOT/src exec python -m llm_search.prompt, which ignores TEXT. Both the keyboard shortcut and the desktop Exec run this.
behaviors.edge_cases: A Rust CLI that calls ActivateAction or Activate directly must pass the same activation-token and desktop-startup-id platform data.

behaviors.behavior: --dry-run: run() prints '  would run: <cmd>' instead of running it; render prints '  would render <name>'; the env file is not written and the safety check is skipped. Read-only gsettings get calls still run, and the 'linked', 'removed old' and 'removed' messages are still printed.
install.sh runs exec <dir of the real install.sh>/bin/llm-search install "$@", so every install option passes through and LLM_SEARCH_HOME is honored.
The provider service file: '[D-BUS Service]', 'Name=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider', 'Exec=/usr/bin/env PYTHONPATH=@SRC@ LLM_SEARCH_HOME=@HOME@ @PYTHON@ -m llm_search'.
behaviors.edge_cases: In Rust the Exec becomes the binary, keeping LLM_SEARCH_HOME=@HOME@. The Name and the file name must not change.

behaviors.behavior: The prompt box service file: '[D-BUS Service]', 'Name=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch', 'Exec=/usr/bin/env PYTHONPATH=@SRC@ LLM_SEARCH_HOME=@HOME@ @PYTHON@ -m llm_search.prompt --gapplication-service'.
behaviors.edge_cases: Keep --gapplication-service.

behaviors.behavior: The desktop file: Type=Application; Name=@CATEGORY@; Comment=Send a prompt to Claude, local models and other AI agents; Icon=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch; Exec=@BIN@ prompt; DBusActivatable=true; Categories=Utility;; Keywords=AI;LLM;Agent;Chat;Prompt;Claude;Spotlight;Launcher;; StartupNotify=true. Its Name is also the search category label.
behaviors.edge_cases: There is no Actions= entry for preferences.

behaviors.behavior: The search provider ini, copied verbatim: '[Shell Search Provider]', DesktopId=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.desktop, BusName=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider, ObjectPath=/io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch/SearchProvider, Version=2. There is no DefaultDisabled, so the provider is on by default.
behaviors.edge_cases: GNOME Shell reads it only from $XDG_DATA_DIRS/gnome-shell/search-providers.

behaviors.behavior: The icon is a scalable 128x128 SVG, copied verbatim and linked as hicolor/scalable/apps/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.svg.

external_contracts: D-Bus name 'io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider', object path '/io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch/SearchProvider', interface org.gnome.Shell.SearchProvider2, with the method names and signatures exactly as in INTERFACE_XML (provider.py:14-41). Metas keys: id, name, description, gicon, all of type 's'.

D-Bus name 'io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch' (the prompt box), object path '/io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch', interfaces org.freedesktop.Application (Activate, ActivateAction) and org.gtk.Actions. Action 'search' takes parameter type 's'; action 'preferences' takes no parameter. Scripts and the provider's LaunchSearch depend on ActivateAction('search', [<s>], {}).

D-Bus service files (symlinks into $XDG_DATA_HOME, default ~/.local/share): dbus-1/services/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider.service (Name=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider) and dbus-1/services/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.service (Name=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch; Exec must accept --gapplication-service). Both bake in LLM_SEARCH_HOME as it was at install time.

Search provider ini: $LLM_SEARCH_HOME/state/xdg/gnome-shell/search-providers/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.search-provider.ini, containing DesktopId=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.desktop, the BusName/ObjectPath above and Version=2.

Desktop file id 'io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.desktop' in ~/.local/share/applications, with DBusActivatable=true, Exec=<~/.local/bin/llm-search> prompt, Icon=io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch and Name = the --name category. GNOME stores this id in the user's org.gnome.desktop.search-providers sort-order/disabled/enabled lists, in favorites and in the app-picker layout. It must also match the Wayland app_id (= the application id).
Icon file: ~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.svg, icon name 'io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch'.

Command path ~/.local/bin/llm-search (a symlink to <code root>/bin/llm-search), plus the 'prompt' subcommand. Existing gsettings shortcut entries store the absolute string '<HOME>/.local/bin/llm-search prompt', and the desktop Exec uses the same path. After the migration, this path must still accept 'prompt [TEXT...]'.

gsettings: org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys custom-keybindings contains '/org/gnome/settings-daemon/plugins/media-keys/custom-keybindings/llm-search/'. At that path, the relocatable schema org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys.custom-keybinding holds name (settings window: 'Agent Search'; installer: the --name value), command '<HOME>/.local/bin/llm-search prompt' and binding (a GTK accelerator string). Users edit it in Settings → Keyboard → Custom Shortcuts.

Config home: $LLM_SEARCH_HOME (default ~/.llm-search), read at runtime by both processes and by the installer. Layout: config/agents.toml (the single source of settings, edited in place with comments kept); config/secrets.env (KEY=value lines, mode 600, key name from [gateway] key_env, default LITELLM_MASTER_KEY); config/settings.toml (0.4.0 legacy, migrated once to settings.toml.migrated); config/.agents.toml.tmp (atomic-save temp file); state/install (rendered files); state/xdg (the extra XDG data dir).

agents.toml keys the settings window writes: [search] min_chars, max_rows; [prompt] idle_minutes; [routing] low_effort_max_words; [[app]] enabled, priority, cwd (addressed by id); [gateway] url, chat_url, auto_model. Also read: [[app]] id, name, url, command (argv with nested optional groups), cwd, requires, description, icon, tags, models, efforts, priority, copy_prompt, enabled; [aliases]; [routing] high_effort_patterns (Python re syntax, case-insensitive) and [[routing.rule]] tag/patterns/weight; [gateway] key_env. Placeholders {prompt}, {model}, {effort}.

~/.config/environment.d/60-llm-search.conf (XDG_CONFIG_HOME honored). It holds exactly '# Added by llm-search: lets GNOME Shell find its search provider.' plus 'XDG_DATA_DIRS=<LLM_SEARCH_HOME>/state/xdg:${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-/usr/local/share/:/usr/share/}'. The installer keeps the file when this exact line is present; uninstall removes any file at that path that contains 'llm-search'.
Path of the systemd environment generator used for the safety check: /usr/lib/systemd/user-environment-generators/30-systemd-environment-d-generator.
--copy install location: $XDG_DATA_HOME/llm-search (default ~/.local/share/llm-search), removed by uninstall --purge.

CLI: llm-search install [--copy] [--dry-run] [--name|--category-name NAME] [--shortcut BINDING]; uninstall [--purge] [--dry-run]; status; query WORDS...; prompt|open [TEXT...]; test; help|-h|--help. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (die), 2 unknown command. ./install.sh [install options] forwards to install. The comments in users' installed agents.toml name `llm-search query` and `llm-search test`.

Environment variables: LLM_SEARCH_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, HOME (shortcut command, ~ expansion, BIN_HOME) and PATH (plus ~/.local/bin and ~/bin for 'requires' lookup). PYTHON is Python-only and can be retired.

Legacy identifiers cleaned on install and uninstall: io.github.oscillatingjem.LlmSearchProvider (.search-provider.ini in state/xdg and ~/.local/share/gnome-shell/search-providers, dbus-1 service, desktop file, svg, state/install/<old>.*), plus the 0.1.0 link ~/.local/share/gnome-shell/search-providers/io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.search-provider.ini.

Output formats that docs and scripts may depend on: 'llm-search status' lines ('  ok      <path>', '  missing <path>', 'search provider: running', 'prompt box: not running (starts when needed)', 'shortcut: <value>' or 'shortcut: none'); 'llm-search query' prints the raw gdbus tuple.

Logs: stderr lines prefixed 'llm-search: ' go to the user journal. The docs grep for 'llm-search', 'LlmSearchProvider' and 'AgentSearch'. The docs and the installer kill processes with `pkill -f llm_search` and `pkill -f -- '-m llm_searc[h]'`, so Rust process names change these instructions.
Docs URLs opened from the settings window: https://github.com/oscillatingjem/gnome-llm-search-provider/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md and .../docs/PROVIDERS.md.

LiteLLM gateway HTTP contract: GET <url>/model/info with an optional 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' header, a 0.5 s timeout, 60 s cache and 30 s back-off. It reads data[].model_name and model_info.{display_name, base, effort, tags, aliases, icon, priority}. Gateway model ids sent to chat_url are '<base>@<effort>'.
python_specific_semantics: toml_edit.format_value writes strings with json.dumps (ensure_ascii=True), so non-ASCII becomes \uXXXX. Characters above the BMP become surrogate pairs ('😀'), which TOML rejects, so saving any value with an emoji fails with EditError. Rust toml_edit writes literal UTF-8, so the bytes in the file differ (and the bug goes away). Checked on Python 3.14.8.

Numbers are written with Python repr: ints as-is, floats as '2.5', '30.0', '1e+16', 'inf', 'nan', '-0.0'. Restore Defaults therefore writes 'idle_minutes = 30.0', while the spin row writes an int ('30'). Rust f64 Display prints 1.0 as '1' (a TOML integer) and NaN as 'NaN' (invalid TOML), so use toml_edit's own formatting.

Read-back verification compares with Python ==, where 1 == 1.0 == True. A Rust check has to decide whether int vs float counts as equal. Python also accepts integers where floats are expected (priority = 1, weight = 3) and floats or bools where ints are expected (min_chars = 3.5 works). Strict serde typing would reject configs that load today.

App(**a) and Rule(**r) dataclasses make unknown or missing keys in [[app]] and [[routing.rule]] fatal (TypeError), while unknown keys elsewhere are ignored. Field types are never checked: a wrong type fails later, at ranking time.

query.parse and prompt-box refresh split with str.split(), which treats Python's whitespace set as separators, including \x1c-\x1f. Rust split_whitespace (Unicode White_Space) does not split on those.

Row.title uses str.capitalize(): the first character is title-cased (e.g. 'ǆ' -> 'ǅ') and the rest lowercased, so 'GPT-4O' becomes 'Gpt-4o'. Rust has no equivalent; implement titlecase first + to_lowercase rest.
@model tokens and [aliases] keys are lowercased with str.lower() (full Unicode mapping including final sigma). Rust to_lowercase is close but should be checked on edge cases.
The agent subtitle slice [:60] counts code points. Rust must slice by chars, not bytes, or it panics on a char boundary.
choose_folder uses str.startswith(home) without a separator check. Keep it or fix it deliberately.
Result ids use hashlib.blake2s(digest_size=6).hexdigest(). The digest size is part of the BLAKE2 parameter block, so truncating BLAKE2s-256 gives a different value.

Routing patterns are Python 're', compiled lazily at every re.search with re.IGNORECASE (Unicode \w, \b, \s by default; lookaround, backreferences, atomic groups and possessive quantifiers since 3.11, conditional groups). An invalid pattern raises on every search instead of at load time. The Rust regex crate has no lookaround or backrefs; fancy-regex is closer but not identical. Python '$' also matches before a trailing newline.

toml_edit (Python) is line-based with str.splitlines(). That converts CRLF files to LF, splits on \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, U+2028 and U+2029 even inside comments and strings, then rejoins with '\n' and adds a final newline. The key regex only matches bare keys, so quoted keys, dotted keys or inline tables cause duplicate-key EditErrors. The Rust toml_edit crate behaves differently on all of these.

URL templates use str.format: '{{' and '}}' escapes, format specs, conversions and index/attribute access all work, and an unknown placeholder raises KeyError. Values are percent-encoded with urllib.parse.quote(safe=''). Then parse_qsl (which decodes '+' to a space) and urlencode(quote_via=quote) re-encode the query and drop empty params, so a literal '+' in a template becomes '%20'.
launch.which uses shutil.which with PATH + ~/.local/bin + ~/bin (an X_OK check). cwd uses os.path.expanduser, which supports '~user'.

Path.read_text() decodes with the locale encoding, effectively UTF-8 on Fedora. A UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, not an OSError, so the settings window's handlers don't catch it. Rust should read UTF-8 explicitly and report the error.

Exceptions raised inside GTK signal handlers are printed by PyGObject and the app keeps running. In Rust a panic in a callback aborts the process, so every launch, save, regex or gateway error must be handled explicitly.

Gio.ThemedIcon.new(name).to_string() returns the bare name, except for names starting with '.' (tokenized form). gio-rs ThemedIcon::to_string has the same behavior, which a hand-rolled string would not.

GLib.Variant('s', text).print_(False) gives the gapplication action argument: single-quoted, or double-quoted when the text contains a single quote. glib::Variant::print(false) is the same C function.

Gtk.accelerator_name with GTK 4.22 gives '<Control><Super>space', not '<Primary>'. gtk4-rs calls the same function, so it matches as long as the same masks are used (accelerator_get_default_mod_mask, keyval_to_lower).
The remove_shortcut bash helper parses gsettings output with Python ast.literal_eval and prints Python list repr. The Rust port should use gio::Settings strv directly.
Python logging.exception writes a multi-line traceback to stderr; Rust will log differently.
Service Exec sets PYTHONPATH, which leaks into every command the provider spawns (env inheritance). It disappears in Rust.
int(minutes*60) and int(spin value) truncate toward zero, and GLib.timeout_add_seconds has 1 s granularity. Use timeout_add_seconds_local in Rust to match.
bugs_or_gaps_found: Values containing characters outside the BMP (emoji in a cwd, URL or model) cannot be saved: json.dumps writes surrogate escapes and tomllib rejects them ('Escaped character is not a Unicode scalar value'), confirmed on Python 3.14.8. (src/llm_search/toml_edit.py:238)

choose_folder turns any path sharing the home prefix into '~…' ('/home/jem2/x' -> '~2/x'). It also crashes with AttributeError when get_path() is None for a non-native or portal folder. (prefs.py:270-273)

The shortcut dialog accepts Shift-only combinations (Shift+A gives '<Shift>a'), which steals normal typing, contradicting the comment at line 356. It rejects bare F-keys, Print and media keys that GNOME Settings allows, and has no conflict detection. (prefs.py:354-358)

The shortcut name diverges: shortcut.set always writes 'Agent Search', while install --shortcut writes the --name value, so changing the binding in settings renames a custom-named entry. The two also order the list update and key writes differently. (shortcut.py:27,39-43 vs bin/llm-search:110-117)

Plausible idle-timer race: open_settings cancels the timer and then hides the prompt window. If notify::is-active fires synchronously during the hide, dismiss() -> start_idle_timer() sees no visible window and arms a timer, or quits at once when idle_minutes <= 0, while the settings window is being opened; that timer is never cancelled. Not verified against GTK's ordering. In Rust, cancel the timer after presenting the settings window. (prompt.py:67,130-132,171-178)

Spin rows save on every notify::value, so each click or step atomically rewrites agents.toml. Values outside a row's range are silently clamped in the UI only. After a failed save the widget keeps showing the unsaved value. (prefs.py:93-102,109-116)
A disabled agent's ExpanderRow cannot be expanded, so its priority and working folder can't be edited until it is switched on. (prefs.py:245-246)

Gateway errors other than OSError/ValueError escape: non-object JSON or non-dict entries raise AttributeError in the provider and in the settings Test button. The fetch blocks the GTK/D-Bus main loop for up to 0.5 s, and in the prompt box this can happen per keystroke after the cache expires. (catalog.py:64-78; prefs.py:320; prompt.py:75)

Uncaught exceptions in GTK handlers: launch failures (missing cwd, no URI handler, unknown {placeholder}), invalid regexes, wrong config types, UnicodeDecodeError, and TOMLDecodeError in app.reload() after an outside edit. PyGObject only prints them; a Rust port must handle each one. (prompt.py:87-96; prefs.py:93-102,194-195)

A bad agents.toml at provider start kills the process before registration, so every search re-activates and fails. A bad edit after start makes every search return D-Bus Failed instead of falling back to the last good config. (provider.py:47-59,101)

Neither LaunchSearch nor ActivateResult passes an activation token or startup id: the prompt box and launched apps may open without focus. The LaunchSearch timestamp is discarded. (provider.py:86-94; launch.py:182-184)

The prompt box can stay resident forever: startup holds the app, and the idle timer is only armed when a window is dismissed or closed. A D-Bus start that never shows a window (introspection, a failed action) therefore never exits. (prompt.py:158,186-194)

Stale docs: USAGE.md says clicking the category icon sends the prompt to the top row, but LaunchSearch opens the prompt box with the query. TROUBLESHOOTING.md says the provider loads config once at start (it reloads when the signature changes) and shows the old id format 'app:claude-chat||'.

The settings window watches only agents.toml: changes to secrets.env or to the gsettings shortcut (e.g. from GNOME Settings) are not reflected while it is open. The (mtime_ns, size) signature misses same-size rewrites within one timestamp tick. The pending 300 ms refresh timer is not removed on close. (prefs.py:41-73; config.py:137-147)

config.update replaces a symlinked agents.toml (dotfiles setups) with a regular file and drops owner and xattrs. set_secret truncates and rewrites in place, not atomically, so a crash mid-write can lose keys. Secret values are written unquoted, and surrounding quotes are stripped on read. (config.py:114-118,121-134,85)

Python toml_edit normalizes CRLF to LF, splits lines on U+2028, \x0c and similar characters inside comments and strings, can match a key line inside a multi-line string or array, and fails with duplicate-key errors when a key is quoted, dotted or in an inline table. (toml_edit.py:260-304)

Installer templating uses sed with unescaped replacements. --name 'Q&A' renders 'Name=Q@CATEGORY@A', a '|' in --name or a path aborts with a sed error, and Desktop Entry escaping is not applied. (bin/llm-search:135-137)

The environment.d check requires a literal ':/usr/share/:' with the trailing slash, so it falsely fails and removes the file on systems whose XDG_DATA_DIRS uses '/usr/share'. It evaluates against the installer's own environment, not a clean login. It is silently skipped on non-systemd systems or when the generator lives at another path. A failing generator exits under set -e without cleanup. Rewriting the file discards any other content. (bin/llm-search:227-246)

Under set -e, a missing g-s-d schema (gsettings present but no media-keys schema) aborts install --shortcut, and aborts uninstall before environment.d removal and pkill, because `list=$(gsettings get …)` fails. remove_shortcut also needs python3 on PATH. (bin/llm-search:108-109,123-126)
Dry runs print 'removed old …', 'removed unused …' and 'removed …' as if the files had been removed. (bin/llm-search:97,249,266)

uninstall without --purge leaves the --copy code ($XDG_DATA_HOME/llm-search) and an empty state/xdg behind, and doesn't refresh the desktop database. status reports dangling symlinks as 'ok' and never checks environment.d or the session's XDG_DATA_DIRS. (bin/llm-search:274-280,291)

'llm-search query' breaks on words that contain a single quote, and with no words it sends ['']. The 'prompt' fallback without gapplication ignores TEXT and uses the env LLM_SEARCH_HOME instead of the installed one. (bin/llm-search:317-320,332-333)

check_requirements never checks the GTK 4 or libadwaita typelibs the prompt box needs, and the Debian hint omits gir1.2-gtk-4.0 and gir1.2-adw-1. --copy copies over an existing directory without removing stale files. (bin/llm-search:44,62-75,164-165)

The 'Keep Running' spin row has digits 0 and truncates fractional idle_minutes from the file on any change. Restore writes 30.0 (float) while the spin writes ints, so the value's TOML type flips between saves. (prefs.py:153-155; config.py:160-162)

Migration hazard: the installer's pkill pattern '-m llm_searc[h]' won't match Rust binaries, and a running legacy Python process keeps owning the bus names (60 s for the provider, up to idle_minutes for the box). The Rust installer must kill both generations. Existing user agents.toml comments point to `python3 -c "import tomllib…"` and `llm-search test`, which a Python-free install may no longer support.

Minimum runtime versions implied by the code: GTK >= 4.12 (CssProvider.load_from_string, FileDialog), libadwaita >= 1.5 (AlertDialog), 1.4 (SpinRow, ToolbarView). gtk4-rs/libadwaita-rs feature flags (v4_12, v1_5) and the MSRV must fit distro rustc (Debian 13: 1.85; Ubuntu 24.04's default rustc is likely too old).

Test coverage gap: none of the 35 tests exercise the D-Bus provider, the prompt box, the settings window, shortcut.py or bin/llm-search. Only the ranker, launch helpers, query parser and config/toml_edit are covered (tests/test_search.py).

facts.finding: gtk4 0.11.5 (2026-09-20) is the latest stable. The 0.11 line started 2026-02-20 (0.11.0) and has had patches 0.11.1 (03-14), 0.11.2 (04-05), 0.11.3 (04-27) and 0.11.4 (06-29). Every 0.11.x declares rust-version 1.92 and edition 2024. Its dependencies are glib/gio/pango/cairo-rs/gdk-pixbuf/graphene ^0.22 and gdk4/gsk4/gtk4-macros ^0.11. The gtk4-rs main branch is already 0.12.0-alpha on gtk-rs-core 0.23.0-alpha, which is not released.
glib and gio 0.22.10 (2026-09-19) are the latest. They declare rust-version 1.92. glib-sys has a baseline system requirement of GLib 2.56, with version features v2_58 through v2_90.

gtk4 0.11.5 has features v4_2 through v4_24, each one cumulative. It also has gnome_42 to gnome_50 SDK alias features. gtk4-sys needs at least GTK 4.0.0, and each feature raises that requirement. The 0.11.0 release notes add v4_22 and gnome_49 and drop the 4.22 save/restore bindings that GTK removed. 0.11.5 reverts an application save/restore feature added in 0.11.2, so APIs can change within 0.11.x patch releases.

libadwaita 0.9.2 (2026-07-07) is the latest. It depends on gtk4/gdk4 ^0.11, glib/gio/pango ^0.22 and libadwaita-sys ^0.9.2. The crate declares no rust-version (null on crates.io), so its effective MSRV is the 1.92 inherited from gtk4/glib. 0.9.0 is yanked. Features: v1_1 through v1_10 (v1_10 is libadwaita 1.10 / GNOME 51), gtk_v4_2 through gtk_v4_24 passthroughs, and gio_v2_80.

No feature gate: Application, ApplicationWindow, Window, HeaderBar, ActionRow, ExpanderRow (show-enable-switch has been there since 1.0), ToastOverlay, ViewStack, ViewSwitcher, PreferencesPage, PreferencesGroup, StatusPage. v1_2: EntryRow (including show-apply-button) and PasswordEntryRow. v1_4: SpinRow and ToolbarView. v1_5: AlertDialog, Dialog and PreferencesDialog. The bindings are AlertDialogExtManual::choose(self, parent, cancellable, callback) and choose_future(self, parent) -> Future<Output=GString>. Gates for newer APIs: Spinner and BottomSheet v1_6; ToggleGroup, WrapBox and InlineViewSwitcher v1_7; ShortcutsDialog and ShortcutLabel v1_8. The minimum flag for the listed set is therefore v1_5.

FileDialog needs v4_10 (open_future, save_future, select_folder_future and the multiple variants). The *_text_file_future variants need v4_18. CssProvider::load_from_string and load_from_bytes need v4_12; load_from_data has been deprecated since 4.12. UriLauncher needs v4_10, and UriLauncher::can_launch needs v4_20. EventControllerKey is GTK 4.0 and needs no flag. ShortcutLabel needs no flag but has been deprecated since GTK 4.18 and will be removed in GTK 5. The minimum flag for the listed Gtk set is v4_12; v4_14 matches Ubuntu 24.04.
GNOME 51, GTK 4.24.0 and libadwaita 1.10.0 shipped in mid-September 2026. Arch extra has gtk4 4.24.1 and libadwaita 1.10.0. Fedora 45 has gtk4 4.24.1 and libadwaita 1.10.0.

In gio 0.22.10, DBusConnection::register_object(path, &DBusInterfaceInfo) returns a RegistrationBuilder. Its methods are method_call(Fn(DBusConnection, Option<&str> sender, &str path, Option<&str> iface, &str method, Variant params, DBusMethodInvocation)), typed_method_call::<T: DBusMethodCall>() (which returns a MethodCallBuilder), property(...), set_property(...) and build() -> Result<RegistrationId, glib::Error>. The builder is !Send.

gtk-rs-core ships examples/gio_dbus_register_object. It parses XML with DBusNodeInfo::for_xml and calls lookup_interface. It uses #[derive(glib::Variant)] argument structs and an enum that implements DBusMethodCall::parse_call. Calls are registered with .typed_method_call::<HelloMethod>().invoke_and_return_future_local(async handler). Registration happens in ApplicationImpl::dbus_register (chained to the parent), and unregistration in dbus_unregister. The example calls app.hold() before run(). The same directory has gio_dbus_object_manager and gio_dbus_receive_signals.

ApplicationImpl provides dbus_register(&self, &DBusConnection, &str) -> Result<(), glib::Error>, dbus_unregister, local_command_line, handle_local_options, command_line, activate, startup and name_lost. ApplicationExtManual::hold() returns an ApplicationHoldGuard that releases on drop, and mark_busy() returns an ApplicationBusyGuard.

zbus 6.0.0 was released on 2026-10-16, two days before this check, with MSRV 1.89. Its breaking changes: the blocking API is removed; zvariant, zbus_names and zbus_utils are folded in; Value is renamed to Variant; the async-io feature is replaced by a zruntime-based default-rt; GVariant support moved to a separate crate; error types are unified. The last 5.x is 5.19.0 (2026-08-09, MSRV 1.87). zbus has no GLib main-loop integration and would open its own session-bus connection, separate from GApplication's GDBusConnection.

search-provider 0.13.0 (2026-02-21) is published by A6GibKm. Its crates.io owners are haecker-felix, bilelmoussaoui and A6GibKm; its repository is gitlab.gnome.org/World/Rust/search-provider. Dependencies: zbus ^5.0 (default-features=false), async-channel and serde, plus optional gdk4 ^0.11 and gdk-pixbuf ^0.22. Features: async-std (default, maps to zbus/async-io) and tokio. SearchProvider::new(imp, bus_name, path) calls zbus::Connection::session().await.unwrap(), serves the object, and requests the given well-known name with ReplaceExisting. Calls go through an async_channel and are handled one at a time by synchronous SearchProviderImpl methods (activate_result, initial_result_set, result_metas). It has no gio::Application, hold/release or inactivity-timeout integration. It is still pinned to zbus 5, not 6.

Use gio directly. Subclass adw::Application. In ApplicationImpl::dbus_register, chain to the parent, then call connection.register_object("/<app/id>/SearchProvider", &iface) with typed_method_call (or method_call for plain Variant handling). Use the app's own bus name, which is the app ID, as BusName in the GNOME Shell search-provider .ini file. In each handler, take `let _g = app.hold();` and reply. Dropping the guard brings the use count back to 0 and restarts the inactivity timeout (call set_inactivity_timeout, e.g. 10_000 ms). This needs no extra connection, bus name, runtime or service file, and D-Bus activation works through GApplication. zbus or search-provider would add a second connection, a second well-known name with its own .service file, and a runtime thread. search-provider also panics if no session bus is available.
facts.source: Design inference from https://docs.rs/gio/latest/gio/struct.RegistrationBuilder.html, the gtk-rs-core example above, and https://docs.gtk.org/gio/class.Application.html (use count reaching zero ends the app; inactivity-timeout is the time to stay alive after becoming idle)

facts.finding: The freedesktop spec says a D-Bus-activatable app implements org.freedesktop.Application with Activate, Open and ActivateAction(name, params, platform-data). The well-known name must equal the desktop-file ID, and the object path is derived from it (dots become slashes). platform-data carries desktop-startup-id and activation-token. In GLib, the D-Bus service file needs Name=<app-id> and Exec=<bin> --gapplication-service (GLib 2.40+). That switch only works if the app keeps the default local_command_line, so never override it and never hard-code IS_SERVICE in flags. IS_SERVICE makes registration fail if an instance is already running. Desktop-file Actions= entries arrive as ActivateAction and map to app actions (gio::ActionEntry, add_action_entries) with the same name, without the app. prefix. gtk-rs does nothing special here: run() passes the process args to GLib's parser. Fedora's Rust-based loupe package ships /usr/share/dbus-1/services/org.gnome.Loupe.service (checked locally).
toml_edit 0.25.17+spec-1.1.0 (2026-10-09, MSRV 1.85) and toml 1.1.8+spec-1.1.0 (2026-10-09, MSRV 1.85) are the latest. Both target the TOML 1.1.0 spec. Fedora 44 packages rust-toml_edit 0.25.17.

Parser behavior: all whitespace and comments before a [table] or [[array]] header become that table's decor prefix, and text after the header on the same line is its suffix. Comments before a key=value become the key's leaf_decor prefix. A same-line trailing comment after a value is the value's decor suffix. Anything left at end of file goes to DocumentMut trailing. So ArrayOfTables::remove(i) takes the comments directly above that [[entry]] header with it. Comment lines after the removed entry's last key belong to the next header's prefix and stay. ArrayOfTables has push, insert, remove, replace, retain, get_mut, iter_mut and into_array. When rendering, a table without a position inherits the last position seen in traversal, so a pushed [[entry]] is emitted right after its preceding sibling, not at end of file.

Array::fmt() collapses an array to single-line style: first value gets the leading default decor, the others the default decor, trailing set to "", and trailing_comma false. Array::push(v) adds the value with only its default decor and does not copy the multi-line layout. To keep a multi-line array, build the value, call value.decor_mut().set_prefix("
    "), then push_formatted, and keep set_trailing("
") and set_trailing_comma(true). Array::remove does not fix up neighbors' decor. What a new table header's default prefix is (believed "
") was not confirmed.

toml::de::Error has message(), span() -> Option<Range<usize>> and set_input(). Its Display output reads 'TOML parse error at line L, column C' followed by a source snippet with a caret. toml::Spanned<T> keeps source ranges. Use #[serde(default)] with impl Default for defaults, and #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to reject typos.

Python 3.14.8 tomllib on this machine rejects TOML 1.1 syntax: newlines inside inline tables, trailing commas in inline tables, times without seconds, and the \e escape. The Rust toml and toml_edit crates accept TOML 1.1, so a config file edited for the Rust build can break the Python build while the two run side by side.

regex 1.13.1 (2026-07-15, MSRV 1.65). fancy-regex 0.19.2 (2026-09-13, MSRV 1.66; default features unicode, perf, std, variable-lookbehinds; Fedora 44 only packages 0.16.2). pcre2 0.2.11 (2025-09-25, no MSRV declared, no release in over a year). glib::Regex wraps GRegex, which always compiles with PCRE2_UCP and adds PCRE2_UTF unless G_REGEX_RAW is set. G_REGEX_OPTIMIZE enables PCRE2 JIT. GLib sets no explicit match limit.

regex is Unicode by default: \d is \p{Nd}, \s is White_Space, \w is Alphabetic + Mark + Nd + Pc + Join_Control, and \b is the Unicode word boundary. (?i) uses simple case folding. There is no lookaround and no backreferences. \A and \z are supported, but \Z is not documented, and {,n} is not documented. \< and \> are word-boundary assertions. Punctuation escapes are allowed for all ASCII except [0-9A-Za-z<>]. Octal escapes work only when enabled. Supported Unicode escapes include \x7F, \x{..}, \u007F, \u{..} and \U0000007F. Named groups can be written (?P<n>) or (?<n>). Nested classes and the &&, -- and ~~ class operators are supported.

fancy-regex adds lookahead and lookbehind (variable-length by default), backrefs (\1, \k<name>, (?P=name)), atomic groups, conditionals, \K, \G, subroutine calls and \Z. Its \Z means end of text before trailing newlines, unlike Python's \Z which is the absolute end. \N means any character except newline, which clashes with Python's \N{NAME}. Patterns without fancy features are delegated to the linear-time regex crate. RegexBuilder has case_insensitive (since 0.14) and backtrack_limit, which defaults to 1,000,000. is_match, find and captures return Result because the backtrack limit can be exceeded. oniguruma_mode(true) makes \< and \> literal but also changes how quantifiers and ^ parse, for example x{2}+ stops being possessive. Version 0.19 uses simple case folding for case-insensitive backreferences.

facts.topic: 5. Python re behaviors to preserve (checked locally with re.IGNORECASE, re.search)
facts.finding: Results from Python 3.14.8: 'a$' matches 'a\n', so $ matches before a final newline. 'a\Z' does not match 'a\n'. \z is accepted in 3.14. \s matches U+001C. \w does not match the combining mark U+0301. (?i)s matches U+017F ſ and (?i)k matches U+212A (Kelvin sign). (?i)[a-z] matches İ (U+0130) and ı (U+0131), and (?i)i matches İ. a{,3}b is valid. \d matches Arabic-Indic digits. Lookbehind, backrefs, atomic (?>..) and possessive a++ work. '\<' matches a literal '<'. '[[]' and '[a&&b]' are literal sets in Python, with FutureWarnings.

facts.finding: Recommend fancy-regex 0.19 with RegexBuilder::new(p).case_insensitive(true).backtrack_limit(N).build(), using is_match as the equivalent of re.search. It is pure Rust, ergonomic and linear-time for most patterns, it bounds backtracking, and it supports lookaround, backrefs, atomic groups and conditionals. Known incompatibilities with Python re: (a) \< and \> are word boundaries, not literals. (b) \Z means 'before trailing newline' in fancy-regex, whereas Python's \Z is the absolute end (Rust's \z). (c) $ only matches at the absolute end; Python also matches before a final \n. (d) [[ inside a class, &&, -- and ~~ are class syntax, not literals. (e) {,n} is likely a compile error. (f) Case folding: İ and ı do not match ASCII i or [a-z]; ſ and K should match in both. (g) \s does not include U+001C..U+001F. (h) \w includes combining marks. (i) \N{NAME} is unsupported, and \N means something else. (j) Octal escapes are off. (k) There are no (?a) or (?L) flags. (l) Match offsets are UTF-8 byte offsets, not code points. (m) Match calls can return BacktrackLimitExceeded. Mitigations: a small pre-translator (\< to <, \> to >, Python \Z to \z, {,n} to {0,n}, escape [ inside classes), and a one-time migration check that compiles every stored user pattern and reports failures. glib::Regex (PCRE2, no new dependency) is closer to Python on \<, nested [ and $, but PCRE2 \Z still differs, \u, \U and \N{} are unsupported, there is no backtracking guard beyond PCRE2's defaults, and the API is less ergonomic. Treat it as the fallback if exact parity matters more than ReDoS safety.

facts.finding: In Rust 1.99.1 std, CommandExt::process_group (stable since 1.64) and pre_exec (stable since 1.34, unsafe) are available. CommandExt::setsid is still nightly-only (process_setsid, issue #105376). Equivalent of Python start_new_session=True: unsafe { cmd.pre_exec(|| { if libc::setsid() < 0 { return Err(io::Error::last_os_error()) } Ok(()) }) } with Stdio::null(). Or use process_group(0) if a new process group is enough, which keeps the posix_spawn fast path. A long-lived service must reap children (wait() in a thread, or glib child watch), or use gio::Subprocess, which reaps automatically.

ureq 3.4.2 (2026-09-13, MSRV 1.85) is blocking and needs no async runtime. Its default features are rustls and gzip. With default-features=false and features=["json"], only plain HTTP is supported, which is enough for localhost: ureq::post(url).send_json(&body)?.body_mut().read_json::<T>()?, with Agent::config_builder().timeout_global(Some(Duration)). Run it in gio::spawn_blocking(f), which returns an awaitable JoinHandle on Gio's I/O pool and should be given a timeout, and await it from glib::MainContext::spawn_local. The alternative is soup3 0.9.0 (2026-03-08, MSRV 1.92, glib/gio ^0.22, features up to v3_8): async on the GLib main loop, but it needs libsoup3-devel to build (Fedora 44 has libsoup3 3.6.6).

facts.finding: #[gtk::test] from gtk4-macros 0.11 wraps #[test] with GTK setup. It runs all tests on one GTK main thread, so they run serially, and it also supports async tests. gtk4-rs's own CI runs `xvfb-run --auto-servernum cargo test` with GSK_RENDERER=cairo in a container. Libadwaita widgets should also call adw::init() (likely).

gio 0.22.10 exposes TestDBus: new(TestDBusFlags), add_service_dir(&str), up(), down(), stop(), bus_address() and unset(). up() starts a private dbus-daemon and sets DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS for the process, so run such tests serially or one per test binary. Point add_service_dir at a generated .service file whose Exec is env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_<bin>") --gapplication-service, then drive org.gnome.Shell.SearchProvider2 with gio::DBusProxy or call_future. The other option is to wrap the test run in `dbus-run-session -- cargo test`. - adw = { package = "libadwaita", version = "0.9.2", features = ["v1_5"] }. v1_5 is needed for AlertDialog; SpinRow and ToolbarView need v1_4; EntryRow and PasswordEntryRow need v1_2. 0.9.0 is yanked.
- glib = "0.22.10", gio = "0.22.10" (MSRV 1.92). No extra GLib feature is needed for the listed APIs.

Raise the flags only if the app really uses newer APIs, and each step drops distros:
- v1_6 adds Spinner and BottomSheet.
- v1_7 adds ToggleGroup, WrapBox and InlineViewSwitcher. This drops Ubuntu 24.04.
- v1_8 adds ShortcutsDialog and AdwShortcutLabel (the replacement for GtkShortcutLabel, deprecated since GTK 4.18). This drops Debian 13.

HTTP: ureq = { version = "3.4.2", default-features = false, features = ["json"] } (MSRV 1.85) plus serde_json, run on gio::spawn_blocking. Alternative: soup3 = "0.9.0" (MSRV 1.92).

Prebuilt-binary baseline that covers every distro above: build on a pinned ubuntu-24.04 runner (glibc 2.39, GTK 4.14.5, libadwaita 1.5.0) with features v4_14 and v1_5.
risks: Ubuntu 24.04 cannot build the current gtk-rs stack with distro rustc. gtk4/glib 0.22/0.11 need Rust 1.92 and noble's newest versioned toolchain is rustc-1.91 (1.91.1). Debian 13 stable has only 1.85.1 and needs trixie-backports (1.96.1). Distro-native packaging on those releases needs rustup, backports, or a downgrade to gtk4 0.10.3 / libadwaita 0.8.1 / glib 0.21.

Compile-time features replace PyGObject's runtime version checks. A binary built with libadwaita v1_7 or newer will not start on Ubuntu 24.04 (libadwaita 1.5.0), and v1_8 or newer will not start on Debian 13 (1.7.6). rustc appears to link with BIND_NOW, so missing symbols fail at load time (likely, not confirmed in rustc source). Pick the feature baseline before porting any UI code.

ubuntu-latest switches to Ubuntu 26.04 between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19. Release binaries built on ubuntu-latest would then silently require glibc 2.43, GTK 4.22 and libadwaita 1.9. Pin runs-on: ubuntu-24.04; GitHub gives no end-of-life date for that image.

zbus 6.0.0 shipped 2026-10-16 with large breaking changes: blocking API removed, Value renamed to Variant, a new runtime, MSRV 1.89. search-provider 0.13.0 is still on zbus ^5, so adopting either means a dependency tree in flux. search-provider also opens a second session connection and calls unwrap() on it, needs its own well-known bus name and .service file, and does not integrate with GApplication hold/release or inactivity timeouts.

If the search provider's object is registered after the bus name is acquired (for example in startup instead of dbus_register), calls from a D-Bus-activated launch could hit a missing object. Register in ApplicationImpl::dbus_register as the gtk-rs example does. Never override local_command_line, or --gapplication-service stops working. Never hard-code ApplicationFlags::IS_SERVICE.

Regex semantics change silently for existing user patterns. Rust regex and fancy-regex differ from Python re on: \< and \> (word boundaries vs literals), \Z, $ before a final newline, [[ and && inside classes, {,n}, Turkish İ/ı case folding, \s on U+001C to U+001F, \w on combining marks, \N{NAME}, octal escapes, the (?a) flag, and byte vs code-point offsets. fancy-regex match calls can also return BacktrackLimitExceeded (default limit 1,000,000). Several Rust-side behaviors were not run because no Rust toolchain is installed here.

TOML 1.1: toml 1.1.8 and toml_edit 0.25.17 accept TOML 1.1 (multi-line inline tables, trailing commas, \e, times without seconds), while Python 3.14 tomllib rejects all four (checked locally). During a phased migration, a config edited by or for the Rust build can break the Python build.

toml_edit decor pitfalls: Array::fmt() collapses multi-line arrays to one line, Array::push does not copy the neighbors' multi-line decor, and Array::remove leaves neighbor decor unchanged. Removing an [[entry]] takes the comments above its header, but the comment lines after its last key stay with the following header. Cover these cases with round-trip golden tests.

gtk4-rs 0.11.x patch releases have added and then reverted APIs (save/restore state added in 0.11.2, reverted in 0.11.5). The main branch is already 0.12.0-alpha on gtk-rs-core 0.23, and a 0.12/0.23 bump around GNOME 52 is likely. Commit Cargo.lock and expect a breaking upgrade roughly every 6 to 12 months.

GtkShortcutLabel has been deprecated since GTK 4.18 and will be removed in GTK 5. AdwShortcutLabel needs libadwaita 1.8 (v1_8), which conflicts with a v1_5 baseline. Expect deprecation warnings once v4_18 or higher is enabled (likely).

Flatpak, the usual way GNOME Rust apps ship (Loupe, Fragments, Shortwave and Pika Backup are all on Flathub), sandboxes the app. Launching detached host processes needs flatpak-spawn --host and talk access to org.freedesktop.Flatpak, which draws scrutiny in Flathub review. A localhost LiteLLM call needs --share=network. Search-provider and D-Bus service files must be exported correctly.

Detached spawning: std CommandExt::setsid is still nightly-only, pre_exec is unsafe and disables the posix_spawn fast path, and a long-lived service process accumulates zombies unless children are reaped.

Search-provider handlers run on the GTK main thread. Slow regex evaluation or blocking HTTP inside GetInitialResultSet stalls both GNOME Shell results and the UI. Bound the work, and use gio::spawn_blocking for blocking I/O.

Test infrastructure: GTK tests run serially on one thread and need a display (xvfb-run, GSK_RENDERER=cairo). gio::TestDBus changes the process-wide DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, so isolate those tests. CI images must include dbus-daemon and Xvfb.

Not verified: openSUSE test-package names (dbus-1-daemon, xvfb-run); Fedora 43 glibc 2.42; the Ubuntu cargo-1.91 package name; whether regex rejects {,n} at compile time; toml_edit's DEFAULT_TABLE_DECOR value; the exact default inactivity behavior of GApplication in service mode; release binary sizes (Fedora installsize figures include data files, so a stripped binary in the low single-digit MB range is only an estimate).
